# Gaussian free-field limits of weighted integer Lipschitz heights

Coordinate `EN-115-000-0003-2-2026-PR-T4-UK-EX-M2-C-ML-H-0460` | `PM-232.1` | status ACTIVE | original slug `Gaussian-free-field-limits-of-weighted-integer-Lipschitz-heights-October-6-2026` | date 2026-10-06 | derived from the openai/math preprint Gaussian-free-field-limits-of-weighted-integer-Lipschitz-heights-October-6-2026, modified (Apache-2.0). ```json
{
  "abstract_verbatim": "We prove a Gaussian free field scaling limit for weighted integer Lipschitz heights on the triangular lattice. With zero boundary values and a factor <i>x</i> for each edge on which the height changes, the field converges after division by a positive constant depending only on <i>x</i> to the zero-Dirichlet Gaussian free field, for every fixed $`x\\in[1/\\sqrt2,1]`$. The convergence holds as a random distribution on every bounded <i>C</i><sup>2</sup> Jordan domain under inside lattice approximations with uniformly convergent boundary parametrizations. This includes the uniform height model and the predicted critical endpoint.",

<a id="pm-s1"></a>
## 1. Abstract and result contract

> We prove a Gaussian free field scaling limit for weighted integer Lipschitz heights on the triangular lattice. With zero boundary values and a factor <i>x</i> for each edge on which the height changes, the field converges after division by a positive constant depending only on <i>x</i> to the zero-Dirichlet Gaussian free field, for every fixed $`x\in[1/\sqrt2,1]`$. The convergence holds as a random distribution on every bounded <i>C</i><sup>2</sup> Jordan domain under inside lattice approximations with uniformly convergent boundary parametrizations. This includes the uniform height model and the predicted critical endpoint.

- **claim-weighted-gff-limit** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thm-main)): For every fixed $x\in[1/\sqrt2,1]$ there exists $\sigma(x)\in(0,\infty)$, independent of $D$ and of the inside approximation in Definition <a href="#def:approximation" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:approximation">1</a>, such that $$\frac{h_\delta}{\sigma(x)}\ \Longrightarrow\ \Phi_D \qquad\text{in }\mathcal D'(D).$$ In particular, the fields are tight as random distributions and, for every $k\ge1$ and $f_1,\ldots,f_k\in C_c^\infty(D)$, the vector $(h_\delta(f_i)/\sigma(x))_{i=1}^k$ converges to $(\Phi_D(f_i))_{i=1}^k$. All mixed moments of these vectors converge.
  - Explanation: Smooth height pairings converge jointly, with all mixed moments, to the zero-Dirichlet Gaussian free field after a positive normalization depending on the fixed edge weight.
- **claim-coherent-spin-lift** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-spin-lift)): Every coherent pair on $G$ has an integer Lipschitz lift, unique up to addition of a multiple of four once the correspondence <a href="#discrete:gray" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="discrete:gray">[discrete:gray]</a> is fixed. For the oriented edge $uv$ its increment is $$\label{discrete:increment} H_v-H_u=\frac{W_uB_v-B_uW_v}{2}.$$ The free spin law induces the weighted height-increment law with one height anchored. Fixing a constant pair on a connected skeleton, and fixing the lift there, induces the usual weighted height Gibbs law in each bounded face of the skeleton.
  - Explanation: Coherent spins determine integrable integer increments. Anchoring their lift identifies the spin law with the weighted height specification.
- **claim-open-cell-factorization** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-lem-cell-cut)): Let $\gamma$ be a simple honeycomb circuit strictly inside the ambient graph. Prescribe $\tau_y=s$ at every $y\in Y\cap\gamma$. Suppose no edge of $E_0$ crosses $\gamma$. Conditional on these prescriptions and any deterministic constraints on the two respective sides, the two sides are independent after their prescribed first-spin layers are identified. On the inside, all cells centered strictly inside retain their original weights; crossing cells contribute constants and impose no condition on $W$. This inside law depends only on $\gamma$, $s$, and the constraints inside. Given the complete height trace of the inside boundary layer, its free sites have the ordinary weighted height Gibbs law, with any additional inside constraints retained.
  - Explanation: Prescribed open crossing cells remove complementary-spin interaction across the circuit, giving an exact conditional separation.
- **claim-annulus-circuit-probability** (bound, [source](#stmt-thm-circuit-input)): For $r\ge0$, let $\Lambda_r$ be the ball of radius $r$ in the triangular graph metric, with its bounding honeycomb contour; thus $\Lambda_r=\Lambda_{\lfloor r\rfloor}$. For $a>1$ and an integer $n\in\mathbb N$, consider on $\Lambda_{an}$ the cell spin law whose interior cells have weight $(x^2)^{\mathbf 1\{B\text{ or }W\text{ nonconstant}\}}$ and whose boundary $Y$ cells are excluded. Fix $B=-$ on the boundary face layer and leave $W$ free. There is $c=c(x,a)>0$ such that, for $n\ge 3/(a-1)$, the probability of an occupied open-plus cell circuit surrounding $\Lambda_n$ and contained in $\Lambda_{an}$ is at least $c$. The same statement holds with the signs or the two spin colors interchanged.
  - Explanation: The excluded-boundary-cell law with adverse first-spin boundary and free complementary spin has a uniformly positive surrounding-circuit probability at admissible scales.
- **claim-restricted-history-order** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-prop-history-order)): For every feasible history, the unobserved $(B,\tau)$ variables are positively associated. Two laws with ordered histories and common $E_0$ are stochastically ordered, including the unequal extreme pins just described. Extra prescribed open-plus cells only in the upper law, or open-minus cells only in the lower law, can be incorporated by observing those cells and all their first-spin sites also in the other law. These claims hold for clipped cells and at $x=1$.
  - Explanation: Complete first-spin observations preserve joint association and order between compatible histories, including clipped cells and the unit-weight endpoint.
- **claim-complementary-partition-lattice** (theorem, [source](#stmt-discrete-ising-partition)): For $a\in[0,1]^E$ define $$\label{discrete:ising-Z} Z(a)=\sum_{\sigma\in\{-,+\}^{V}} \prod_{e=uv\in E}a_e^{\mathbf 1\{\sigma_u\ne\sigma_v\}}, \qquad 0^0=1.$$ Then $Z$ is increasing in every coordinate and is log-supermodular: $$\label{discrete:Z-lattice} Z(a\wedge b)Z(a\vee b)\ge Z(a)Z(b).$$
  - Explanation: The complementary-spin partition sum increases with edge parameters and satisfies the multiplicative lattice inequality, including zero parameters.
- **claim-online-own-history-kernels** (construction, [source](#stmt-discrete-online)): Consider two finite-volume laws ordered as in Proposition <a href="#prop:history-order" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:history-order">6</a>. There is an online exploration coupling with the following invariant: conditional on every full joint query record, the eventual completion in either coordinate has that coordinate’s original Gibbs conditional law given its own observed values and deterministic constraints. The next cell, together with all its first spins, may be chosen as any deterministic function of the joint record. If the retained conditional problems become identical, their completions can be sampled identically.
  - Explanation: Recursive coupling of query blocks preserves each coordinate's own Gibbs conditional marginal at the full joint record.
- **claim-buffered-circuit-stack** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-buffer-circuits)): Fix a finite collection of annuli and tubes in a bounded planar region, each with a positive-width buffer and with prescribed geometric clearance. At mesh $\delta$, suppose the buffers contain no equality edge $E_0$ and no first-spin pin adverse to a requested sign. Then each request for good circuits, or connected good paths formed from a finite annular chain, has probability bounded below by a positive constant independent of $\delta$ for all sufficiently small $\delta$. The bound is uniform over feasible histories supported away from the buffers and over lattice translations preserving the clearances. Requests with the same sign may be combined by association; requests of different signs in disjoint buffers may be made successively. In an annular stack of fixed-ratio, separated slots between lattice scales $r$ and $L$, the probability of finding no requested good circuit is at most $$\label{discrete:stack} C(r/L)^\alpha,$$ for constants $C,\alpha>0$.* *Moreover, conditioning a free ambient law on any deterministic collection of open-plus cells and their first-spin values increases every increasing event in $(B,\tau)$. This applies to a favorable path event in the ambient plane even when its path leaves the interior of a prescribed good contour.
  - Explanation: Filled comparison disks and intersecting annular chains provide favorable paths with fixed positive probability; successive separated slots give a power-law failure bound.
- **claim-free-plane-local-matching** (bound, [source](#stmt-prop-local-mixing)): There are $C,\alpha>0$ with the following property. Suppose a finite ambient graph contains a ball of radius $L$ together with its interaction cells, and its law has first-spin pins and second-spin equalities, none in that ball. Then its pair marginal in the concentric radius-$r$ ball is within $C(r/L)^\alpha$ in total variation of a common free plane law, for $L\ge Cr\ge C$. The same is true with the statuses of either fixed choice of first color. The plane law is the local limit of free ambient laws along every exhaustion, and its unaugmented pair and increment laws preserve translations, lattice symmetries, and height symmetries.* *Adding extreme first-spin pins in a bounded inner region can be coupled to the original law so that the configurations agree beyond a common circuit of the added sign. If there are $k$ separated favorable annular slots outside all the changes and no adverse pins or equality edges in their buffers, the failure probability is at most $Ce^{-ck}$. All matches preserve the individual conditional marginals at every joint record as in Lemma <a href="#discrete:online" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="discrete:online">9</a>.
  - Explanation: Common stopped circuits couple local marginals to a unique free-plane limit. Added extreme pins can be screened from the exterior.
- **claim-record-independent-plane-copy** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-cor-conditional-plane-matching)): Let $\mathcal R$ be an exterior record, and let $G$ be its successful-search event, determined by that record. Suppose that on every successful record a good circuit surrounds $B(z,L)$ together with its interaction cells, and that conditional on this record the retained law is the open-cut law of Lemma <a href="#lem:cell-cut" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:cell-cut">4</a>, with no additional inside pins or equality edges. For $L\ge Cr\ge C$, the pair variables in $B(z,r)$ can be coupled with variables $P_r$ of the fixed free-plane marginal $\nu_r$ so that $$\mathbb P(P_r\in A\mid\mathcal R)=\nu_r(A) \quad\text{for every event }A, \qquad \mathbb P(\text{mismatch}\mid\mathcal R)\le C(r/L)^\alpha \quad\text{on }G.$$ The same plane marginal is assigned on failure. Consequently $P_r$ is independent of the entire record and the total mismatch probability is at most $\mathbb P(G^c)+C(r/L)^\alpha$. Agreement of pair variables also matches increments along paths contained in $B(z,r)$.
  - Explanation: Recordwise coupling to the same plane marginal yields a plane copy independent of the exterior record, with search failure and local mismatch accounting for the error.
- **claim-separated-pin-products** (bound, [source](#stmt-prop-rare-pins)): Fix $k$ bounded filled simply connected neighborhoods $U_1,\ldots,U_k$ with disjoint closures. In each $U_i$ let $P_i$ prescribe arbitrary first spins on a finite site set and prescribe second-spin plus on at most $m_i$ connected lattice subgraphs, singletons allowed. Assume the supports stay a fixed positive distance from $\partial U_i$, so that isolating circuit collars fit inside $U_i$, and let $m=\sum_i m_i$ be fixed. In the free plane law, $$\label{discrete:rare-pins} c\prod_{i=1}^k\mathbb P(P_i) \le \mathbb P\Bigl(\bigcap_{i=1}^kP_i\Bigr) \le C\prod_{i=1}^k\mathbb P(P_i).$$ The constants depend on $x$, $k$, $m$, and the fixed buffers, but not on the numbers of pinned sites, the lengths of the connected subgraphs, or lattice translations preserving the buffers. The comparison also holds in finite free ambient volumes containing all the required comparison collars. Previous pins inside the currently considered obstacle are retained in both comparison laws.
  - Explanation: Separated pin probabilities admit multiplicative comparison even when they are rare. Constants depend on fixed buffers and connected label requests rather than the number of pinned sites.
- **claim-protected-component-switch** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-collar-switch)): Suppose two nested good circuits have opposite first-spin signs. Between and on the two circuits assume there are no second-spin equality constraints or prescribed second-spin labels. Conditional on the first spins and cell statuses, there is a deterministically selectable second-spin component in that collar whose fair label flip changes the integer lift throughout the protected inner region by $+4$ or $-4$ relative to the protected exterior, while preserving both spins in both protected regions. The selection uses only the first spins, statuses, equality edges, and the two circuits. It therefore preserves any stopped selection of the circuits based on these data.* *For disjoint collars the switches commute and give equally weighted orbits containing every parity vector of the corresponding inner lift offsets in $4\mathbb Z$. Spin constraints and comparisons of lifts along paths inside the protected regions are preserved. With the height anchor fixed in the protected exterior, a test supported there is unchanged; a zero-total test supported entirely in the protected inner region is also unchanged. Opposite good cuts can be required in any fixed nested pin-free collars with uniformly positive probability. The assertion holds with the two colors interchanged.
  - Explanation: An unlabelled complementary component between opposite cuts can be flipped to change a protected integer offset while keeping protected spins and zero-total observations unchanged.
- **claim-height-order-flat-loops** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-height-order)): Let the free sites be in bounded faces of a connected triangular-lattice skeleton of fixed integer trace. Include all neighbors of free sites up to that trace. The weighted height law is positively associated, and ordered feasible traces give stochastically ordered laws. The assertion also applies after restricting to components separated by further fixed curves. With constant trace, the changing dual edges are disjoint closed honeycomb loops. Given their unoriented geometry their jumps are independent fair signs. Exposing such loops from the outside leaves in each unexposed interior the empty-exterior loop law with the appropriate constant inner boundary layer.
  - Explanation: Convex edge energies give height association and trace order. Constant traces give closed loops with conditionally independent fair jumps and stopped interior factorization.
- **claim-shell-loop-tails** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-shell-moments)): In a finite constant-boundary height problem, let $N_d(z)$ be the number of level loops surrounding a site $z$ whose Euclidean closest approach to $z$ belongs to $[d,2d)$, where $d\geq1$. There are $c,C>0$ such that $$\label{moments:shell-tail} \mathbb P\{N_d(z)\geq t\}\leq Ce^{-ct}\qquad(t\geq0).$$ In particular, for each finite $p\geq1$, $\mathbb EN_d(z)^p\leq C_p$. These constants are independent of the shape, $z$, and $d$, and the same assertions hold in any bounded face of a connected flat skeleton.
  - Explanation: Repeated stopped-loop explorations encounter a uniform obstruction, producing exponential tails for shell counts without assumptions on the flat skeleton's shape.
- **claim-common-loop-covariance** (bound, [source](#stmt-moments-covariance)): Let the flat trace be zero, let $n$ be the distance from $z_0$ to its bounding skeleton, and let $z,w\in B(z_0,a)$, where $1\leq a\leq c_0n$ for a sufficiently small absolute $c_0$. With $b=\max(1,\|z-w\|)$, $$\label{moments:covariance-bound} 0\leq\mathbb E[H(z)H(w)] \leq C\left(1+\log\frac{n}{b}\right).$$ Every smearing <a href="#moments:weights" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="moments:weights">[moments:weights]</a> in this ball therefore satisfies $$\label{moments:second-moment} \mathbb EY^2\leq C A^2\left(1+\log\frac{n}{a}\right).$$
  - Explanation: Independent loop jumps identify covariance with the expected number of common enclosing loops. Shell and arm estimates then control covariance and signed smearings.
- **claim-discrete-midpoint-sums** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thm-midpoint)): Let $f,g,u,v:\mathbb Z^m\longrightarrow[0,\infty)$ have finite support, and write $m_-(s,t)=\lfloor(s+t)/2\rfloor$ and $m_+(s,t)=\lceil(s+t)/2\rceil$, with coordinatewise rounding. If, for every $s,t\in\mathbb Z^m$, $$f(s)g(t)\leq u(m_-(s,t))v(m_+(s,t)),$$ then $$\left(\sum f\right)\left(\sum g\right) \leq\left(\sum u\right)\left(\sum v\right).$$
  - Explanation: A pointwise rounded-midpoint product inequality implies the corresponding inequality between total sums for nonnegative finitely supported arrays.
- **claim-weighted-midpoint-admissibility** (theorem, [source](#stmt-moments-weighted-midpoints)): Let $\mathcal S$ be the integer $1$-Lipschitz arrays on a finite connected graph, with fixed integer heights on a nonempty set of vertices. Set $$\mathcal W(h)=\mathbf 1_{\{h\in\mathcal S\}} x^{\sum_{\{i,j\}}\|h_i-h_j\|}.$$ Then $\mathcal S$ is finite, both rounded midpoints of $s,t\in\mathcal S$ belong to $\mathcal S$, and $$\label{moments:weight-midpoint} \mathcal W(m_-(s,t))\mathcal W(m_+(s,t))\geq \mathcal W(s)\mathcal W(t).$$ Moreover a linear statistic with $\sum\|w_i\|\leq A$ obeys $$\label{moments:rounding} \left\|Y(m_\pm(s,t))-\frac{Y(s)+Y(t)}2\right\|\leq A/2.$$ The same energy inequality holds with additional support constraints whenever both outputs satisfy those constraints.
  - Explanation: Rounded midpoints preserve integer Lipschitz constraints and fixed integer coordinates, improve the product weight, and incur a bounded linear-statistic rounding error.
- **claim-class-central-amplification** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-midpoint-amplification)): Let $\mu(h)=\mathcal W(h)/Z$ be a finite probability measure on integer arrays. Partition its support into at most $J$ classes. Suppose that two arrays from the same class have both rounded midpoints in the full support, with the weight inequality <a href="#moments:weight-midpoint" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="moments:weight-midpoint">[moments:weight-midpoint]</a>. Let $Y$ be a linear statistic satisfying <a href="#moments:rounding" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="moments:rounding">[moments:rounding]</a>. If $M>0$, $M\geq A/2$, and, for every class $\mathcal S_i$, $$\label{moments:class-central} \mu\bigl(\mathcal S_i\cap\{\|Y\|\leq M\}\bigr)\geq c>0,$$ then there are $a_*>0$ and $C_p<\infty$, depending only on $J,c,p$, such that $$\label{moments:amplification} \mu\{\|Y\|>tM\}\leq4e^{-a_*t}\quad(t\geq0), \qquad \\|Y\\|_{L^p(\mu)}\leq C_pM\quad(1\leq p<\infty).$$ Outputs may belong to any class. In particular no stability of an individual class under midpoint rounding is required.
  - Explanation: Positive unconditional central mass in every input class and admissible same-class midpoints imply exponential tails and finite-moment bounds; outputs need not remain in their input class.
- **claim-bounded-trace-smearing** (bound, [source](#stmt-prop-smearing)): In a bounded height problem as specified above, suppose its fixed trace has absolute value at most $K$. Let $n$ be the distance from the smearing center to the bounding sites. For $1\leq a\leq c_0n$ and every finite $p\geq1$, $$\label{moments:smearing-bound} \left\\|\sum_uw_uH(u)\right\\|_p \leq C_{p,A}\left(1+K+\sqrt{\log(n/a)}\right).$$ The bound is uniform over the shape of the trace and applies in particular to the interior of a good cut after its complete inner height layer has been specified.
  - Explanation: Flat covariance control and midpoint amplification bound all finite smearing moments; height order extends the bound to bounded irregular traces.
- **claim-plane-zero-total-moments** (bound, [source](#stmt-prop-plane-moments)): For the infinite-volume increment law furnished by Proposition <a href="#prop:local-mixing" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:local-mixing">11</a>, every zero-total smearing <a href="#moments:weights" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="moments:weights">[moments:weights]</a> satisfies $$\label{moments:plane-bound} \left\\|\sum_uw_uH(u)\right\\|_p\leq C_{p,A} \qquad(1\leq p<\infty).$$ The constants are uniform in $a\geq1$ and the center. The same estimate holds for the increment law in a finite free simply connected triangulation containing $B(z_0,C_0a)$, for a sufficiently large fixed $C_0$.
  - Explanation: Zero-total smearings have uniformly bounded finite moments in the free plane and sufficiently large free finite volumes, independently of their additive lift.
- **claim-two-disk-nondegeneracy** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-nondegeneracy)): Let $U_1,U_2$ be two fixed disjoint round disks with disjoint closures, and let $f_i\geq0$ be smooth functions supported compactly in $U_i$, with $\int f_i=1$. Form their exact face-area averages on the dilated lattice geometry of scale $R$. If $Y_R$ is the first average minus the second, there is $c>0$ such that $$\label{moments:nondegeneracy} \mathbb EY_R^2\geq c$$ for all sufficiently large $R$, in the plane and in sufficiently large finite free volumes. The bound is uniform under translations of the fixed arrangement.
  - Explanation: A protected fair component switch shifts one disk's unit average relative to the other, giving a positive second-moment lower bound.
- **claim-plane-green-covariance** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prop-plane-covariance)): There is a constant $v=v(x)\in(0,\infty)$, depending only on the fixed weight $x$, such that for every pair of real zero-integral tests $f,g\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2)$, $$\begin{aligned} \lim_{\delta\downarrow0}\mathbb E[H_\delta(f)H_\delta(g)] &=\frac{v}{(2\pi)^2} \int_{\mathbb R^2}\frac{\widehat f(p)\overline{\widehat g(p)}}{\|p\|^2} \,\mathrm dp \label{plane:eq:covariance}\\ &=\frac{v}{2\pi}\iint_{\mathbb R^2\times\mathbb R^2} f(z)\log\frac1{\|z-w\|}\,g(w)\,\mathrm dz\,\mathrm dw. \notag \end{aligned}$$ The conclusion also holds for zero-integral tests converging in $C_c^\infty$ with a common compact support.
  - Explanation: Exact-area covariances converge to a positive Euclidean Green form with a coefficient fixed solely by the edge weight, also for smoothly varying zero-integral tests.
- **claim-positive-normal-transfer** (construction, [source](#stmt-prop-reflection-transfer)): Let $\ell$ be any row of lattice sites parallel to one of the three unoriented nearest-neighbor directions, and choose one of its closed half-planes. The plane pair is reflection positive across $\ell$. The assertion remains valid after adjoining any finite collection of fields $$\label{plane:eq:phases} Z_s(u)=U_s\exp\{is(H(u)-H(o))\},$$ where the $U_s$ are independent unit-circle Haar variables, independent of the pair, and $o$ is any anchor.* *More precisely, let $\theta_\ell$ act on observables by spatial reflection, and take local functions supported in the chosen half-plane, whose height differences are evaluated along paths in that half-plane. Then $$\langle F,G\rangle_\ell =\mathbb E\big[\overline{\theta_\ell F}\,G\big]$$ is a positive semidefinite Hermitian form. In its quotient completion, translation farther into the half-plane by the pure normal vector of length $\sqrt3$ is a positive self-adjoint contraction $S$. Unit translation along the row is a commuting unitary $U$. At mesh $\delta$ the normal step is $\sqrt3\delta$.
  - Explanation: Conditioning on a site row establishes reflection positivity, including Haar phases. Pure normal translation descends to a positive contraction and commutes with tangential unitary translation.
- **claim-punctured-increment-spectrum** (construction, [source](#stmt-plane-lem-spectrum)): There is a positive, locally finite measure $C$ on $\widehat\mathbb T\setminus\{0\}$, invariant under the lattice rotations and reflections, such that every finitely supported real array $(b_u)$ with $\sum b_u=0$ satisfies $$\label{plane:eq:spectrum} \mathbb E\left\|\sum_u b_uH(u)\right\|^2 =\int\left\|\sum_u b_ue^{ip\cdot u}\right\|^2 C(\,\mathrm dp).$$ There is no invariant random linear tilt term. Moreover, for some $r_0>0$ and $K<\infty$, $$\label{plane:eq:annuli} C\{r\le\|p\|\le2r\}\le K\quad(0<r<r_0), \qquad \int_{0<\|p\|<r_0}\|p\|^t C(\,\mathrm dp)<\infty\quad(t>0).$$
  - Explanation: Scalar translation measures and the increment cocycle define a punctured spectral measure. Uniform zero-total moments exclude invariant linear tilt and bound small spectral annuli.
- **claim-positive-cauchy-mixture** (construction, [source](#stmt-plane-lem-mixture)): On $k\ne0$ in the rectangular torus there is a positive measure $\nu(\,\mathrm dk,\,\mathrm ds)$ such that $$\label{plane:eq:mixture} C'(\,\mathrm dk,\,\mathrm dl)=\int_{[0,\infty]}Q_s(\,\mathrm dl)\,\nu(\,\mathrm dk,\,\mathrm ds).$$ The measure $\nu$ is finite on horizontal bands bounded away from zero, and, for every sufficiently small fixed $\kappa>0$, $$\label{plane:eq:weighted-nu} \int_{0<\|k\|<\kappa}\|k\|\,\nu(\,\mathrm dk,\,\mathrm ds)<\infty.$$ The physical punctured line $k=0$ near zero has zero $C$ mass, and $C\{a_*\}=0$. These conclusions hold before any rescaling limit is taken. The analogous assertions hold in each of the three rotated charts.
  - Explanation: The positive normal transfer represents the projected spectrum as a Cauchy mixture. Rotated charts rule out physical tangential-line mass and the nonzero alias atom.
- **claim-angular-defect-summability** (bound, [source](#stmt-plane-lem-defect)): Uniformly for $s\in[0,\infty]$ and sufficiently small $k\ne0$, $$\label{plane:eq:poisson} \int\chi(k,l)Q_s(\,\mathrm dl)=D(k,s)+O(\|k\|).$$ For some fixed $\kappa>0$, $$\label{plane:eq:defect} \int_{0<\|k\|<\kappa}D(k,s)\,\nu(\,\mathrm dk,\,\mathrm ds)<\infty.$$ There is also $K_1<\infty$ such that, for all sufficiently small $r>0$, $$\label{plane:eq:bands} \nu\{r\le\|k\|\le2r\}\le K_1.$$
  - Explanation: The angular Poisson identity and rotational cancellation make the nonnegative dispersion defect integrable and control horizontal mixing bands.
- **claim-spectral-endcap-control** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-endcaps)): After decreasing $r_0$ if necessary, there is $K_3<\infty$ such that $$\label{plane:eq:endcaps} C\{b<\|p\|\le2b,\ \|k\|\le h\}\le K_3\frac hb \qquad(0<b<r_0,\quad0<h<b/10).$$ The same bound holds in each rotated chart. In particular, rescaling cannot create mass on one of the tangential zero lines inside a compact punctured annulus.
  - Explanation: Rotating narrow endcaps into nonzero normal frequencies bounds their mass and prevents rescaled concentration on tangential zero lines.
- **claim-isotropic-subsequential-spectrum** (classification, [source](#stmt-plane-lem-subsequences)): Every vague subsequential limit is $$\label{plane:eq:subsequence} M(\,\mathrm dp)=c\frac{\,\mathrm dp}{\|p\|^2}$$ for some finite $c\ge0$, at this point possibly depending on the subsequence. This identity holds on the entire punctured plane, including the tangential zero lines.
  - Explanation: Summable defect concentrates limiting Cauchy mixtures on their isotropic dispersion relation; independent mirror directions force an inverse-square spectral density.
- **claim-unique-spectral-coefficient** (theorem, [source](#stmt-plane-lem-unique)): There is a single $c\ge0$ such that $C_\delta$ converges vaguely to $c\,\mathrm dp/\|p\|^2$ as $\delta\downarrow0$.
  - Explanation: A scalar signed-cutoff limit fixes the same spectral coefficient for every subsequence, giving full vague convergence.
- **claim-reflection-null-insertion** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-prop-reflection-null)): Fix one of the three row directions. Let $\ell_\delta$ be site rows of $\delta\mathbb T$ converging to a line $\ell$ in that direction, and choose the same side of each row. Suppose that real $\varphi_\delta\to\varphi$ in $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2)$, with common compact support lying on that side at a positive distance from $\ell_\delta$ for all sufficiently small $\delta$. Put $X_\delta=H_\delta(\Delta\varphi_\delta)$, using exact area weights. Then $$\label{plane:eq:reflection-null} \\|X_\delta\\|_{\ell_\delta}^2 =\mathbb E[(\theta_{\ell_\delta}X_\delta)X_\delta] \longrightarrow0, \qquad \sup_{\delta\text{ small}}\\|X_\delta\\|_{L^2}<\infty.$$ This holds also in every finitely phase-augmented reflection space of Proposition <a href="#prop:reflection-transfer" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:reflection-transfer">25</a>. In particular, if $Y_\delta$ is supported on the same side and has bounded reflection norm, then $\mathbb E[(\theta_{\ell_\delta}Y_\delta)X_\delta]\to0$.
  - Explanation: A Laplace test separated from its reflection has vanishing reflection seminorm, while ordinary second moments stay bounded.
- **claim-inner-boundary-walk** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-boundary-walk)): There is a closed walk $S_{0,\delta}$ of adjacent triangular-lattice face centers, with repeated vertices and edges allowed, whose vertex set is exactly the boundary face layer $\partial F_\delta$. Its parametrized trace is within $O(\delta)$ of the boundary cycle in traversal order. Every free interior site lies in a bounded face of this walk, with winding number one, and every interaction path from a free interior site to an exterior site meets its vertex set.* *For small $\delta$, $\pi$ is defined on the walk, its degree is one, and the following fixed-scale assertions hold. For each $b>0$, the number of subwalks with disjoint traversal-time interiors and projected diameter at least $b$ is bounded independently of sufficiently small $\delta$. Every proper projected boundary arc is traversed from end to end by a subwalk, up to $o(1)$ errors at its endpoints. These assertions do not require a bound on the length of $S_{0,\delta}$ or on its number of crossings of a line.
  - Explanation: Traversal of the honeycomb boundary produces a separating face-center walk. Parametric convergence controls fixed-size projected excursions without bounding microscopic walk length.
- **claim-bounded-boundary-label-count** (bound, [source](#stmt-pins-label-count)): At fixed $\mathcal L$ and $\epsilon$, the number of connected components used to form $A_{\delta,\epsilon}$ is bounded by a constant $M(\mathcal L,\epsilon)$ independent of sufficiently small $\delta$.
  - Explanation: Retained boundary components require disjoint macroscopic traversal excursions, so their label count stays bounded at fixed grid and window geometry.
- **claim-integer-bracket-order** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-pins-bracket-order)): The bracket traces are actual integer heights satisfying $$\label{pins:trace-intervals} H_\delta^{+,\epsilon}\in\{0,1\},\qquad H_\delta^{-,\epsilon}\in\{-1,0\} \quad\hbox{on }S_{0,\delta},\qquad H_\delta^{\pm,\epsilon}=0\quad\hbox{on }A_{\delta,\epsilon}.$$ Conditional on either trace, the free interior has the original weighted height Gibbs law. There is an ordered coupling $$\label{pins:height-sandwich} H_\delta^{-,\epsilon}\le h_\delta\le H_\delta^{+,\epsilon}$$ on every interior face. The bounded-trace smearing estimates of Proposition <a href="#prop:smearing" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:smearing">21</a> apply to both brackets with constants independent of the window sizes.
  - Explanation: Connected constant-color boundary pins fix actual integer pairs. Their Gibbs interiors can be ordered around the true zero-boundary field.
- **claim-marker-lift-checks** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-pins-marker-checks)): For every fixed $a,\epsilon$ and separated placement of the groups, $$\label{pins:check-success} \mathbb P(P_{\mathrm{loc}}\mid P)\longrightarrow1.$$ The assertion holds also after any fixed rigid translations or lattice reflections of the groups, and along converging placements that retain the specified positive clearances.
  - Explanation: Good circuits around projected markers join all retained pinned chains, making their common lifted-pair checks asymptotically successful.
- **claim-checked-rare-pin-moments** (bound, [source](#stmt-prop-pin-moments)): Consider any of the fixed separated arrangements above, including arrangements enlarged by reflected copies. Let $Y_\delta=H_\delta(f)$, where $f$ is a real smooth zero-integral test supported in a disk having a filled cut-search neighborhood disjoint from all $U_i$. For every $1\le p<\infty$, $$\label{eq:pin-moments} \mathbb E\bigl[\|Y_\delta\|^p\mid P_{\mathrm{loc}}\bigr]\le C_p$$ for all sufficiently small $\delta$. The constants are uniform on compact families of such arrangements with positive clearances and bounded smooth test norms. The same holds for finite collections of these tests and, by separating real and imaginary parts, for complex tests.
  - Explanation: A parity partition, protected switches, and central mass in every class justify midpoint amplification after checked rare conditioning.
- **claim-normalized-side-reflection-bound** (bound, [source](#stmt-pins-side-norm)): Suppose a family of checked obstacles and factors lies strictly on one side of a site row. Their filled neighborhoods and all needed check paths lie on that side; unbounded factors have free test neighborhoods disjoint from the obstacle neighborhoods. If $A$ is a bounded product, possibly including arbitrary Haar phases, times at most one smooth zero-total insertion, then $$\label{pins:normalized-side-bound} \left\\|A\prod_i\frac{\mathbf 1_{P_i\cap C_i}}{p_{i,\delta}} \right\\|_\vartheta\le C.$$ The bound is uniform on compact families with the stated margins.
  - Explanation: Multiplicative rare-pin comparisons cancel the normalization in a doubled reflected arrangement, while checked moments control the optional insertion.
- **claim-analytic-translation-backoff** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-lem-analytic-translation)): Partition a finite arrangement of the preceding checked obstacles and local factors into two families separated strictly in projection on a lattice reflection normal $n$. At most one factor is an unbounded zero-total insertion. Translate the high family by $sn$, and let $M_\delta(s)$ be its plane expectation normalized by the product $J_\delta$ of all individual ordinary pin probabilities, at lattice normal-step translations. If $$M_\delta(s_\delta)\longrightarrow0$$ for every $s$ in a nonempty open interval $I\subset(0,\infty)$ and every lattice rounding $s_\delta\to s$, then $M_\delta(0)\to0$. The same is true for a low family translated by $-sn$, and along any converging sequence of other placements preserving the required margins.
  - Explanation: Positive transfer spectra provide bounded holomorphic continuations on a domain containing the original placement; vanishing on an open translation interval forces vanishing there.
- **claim-local-separating-grid** (construction, [source](#stmt-pins-local-geometry)): Fix $z_0\in D$, $\overline{B(z_0,\rho)}\subset D$, and an integer $q\ge0$. One can choose a finite grid of regular horizontal levels, depending only on $z_0,\rho,q$, with the following property. If $K_0\subset B(z_0,\rho/1000)$ and at most $q$ spectator disks of radii less than $\rho/(1000(q+1))$ lie outside $B(z_0,\rho)$, two grid levels give all the strict geometry in <a href="#pins:middle-geometry" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="pins:middle-geometry">[pins:middle-geometry]</a>. The same grid works for any finite number of such collections of spectator disks.
  - Explanation: A finite regular-level grid supplies separating levels for sufficiently small insertion and distant spectator disks, with an oblique middle-strip split.
- **claim-separated-phase-insertion** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-pins-three-moves)): At fixed positive gaps satisfying <a href="#pins:middle-geometry" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="pins:middle-geometry">[pins:middle-geometry]</a>, and for any product $\Psi_\delta$ of local Haar-phase factors at the representatives with fixed frequencies, $$\label{pins:separated-identity} J_\delta^{-1}\mathbb E\left[ X_\delta F_\delta\Psi_\delta\mathbf 1_{P_{\mathrm{loc}}}\right] \longrightarrow0.$$ This holds for every converging lattice-rounded sequence of placements with the stated strict separations.
  - Explanation: Successive outward motions separate all factors from the insertion; reflection-null control and reverse analytic continuation return the vanishing identity to the original placement.
- **claim-gap-closing-common-offsets** (bound, [source](#stmt-pins-gap-closing)): There is a function $\omega(a)\to0$ as $a\downarrow0$ such that $$\begin{aligned} \limsup_{\delta\downarrow0} \mathbb P(P_=^c\mid P)&\le\omega(a), \label{pins:offset-synchronization}\\ \limsup_{\delta\downarrow0} \left\\|\mu_{\delta,a}^{=}\|_{\mathcal I_\delta} -\mu_{\delta,0}\|_{\mathcal I_\delta}\right\\|_{\mathrm{TV}} &\le\omega(a),\label{pins:increment-tv}\\ \limsup_{\delta\downarrow0} \mathbb E_{\mu_{\delta,a}^{=}}\|X_\delta\|^p &\le C_p\qquad(1\le p<\infty), \label{pins:uniform-common-moments} \end{aligned}$$ where $\mathcal I_\delta$ is the joint increment information in the fixed test disks. The constants in the last line are independent of all sufficiently small $a$.
  - Explanation: Circuit stacks synchronize neighboring integer offsets and couple local increments to the filled bracket. A separate central-mass argument controls moments uniformly as gaps close.
- **claim-filled-bracket-insertion** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-prop-bracket-insertion)): Fix a grid, windows, and local factors as in <a href="#pins:insertion-data" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="pins:insertion-data">[pins:insertion-data]</a>. Suppose two grid levels strictly bracket $K_0$, miss every spectator disk, and give the strict middle-strip geometry <a href="#pins:middle-geometry" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="pins:middle-geometry">[pins:middle-geometry]</a> for the boundary groups after arbitrarily small intersection gaps are opened. Then both filled brackets satisfy the target identity <a href="#eq:bracket-insertion" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:bracket-insertion">[eq:bracket-insertion]</a>. In particular, any subsequential distributional bracket limit with convergent local test statistics satisfies the corresponding identity against products of bounded continuous functions of those statistics.
  - Explanation: Common-offset phase projection, gap comparison, and uniform truncation control transfer the separated insertion identity to both filled brackets.
- **claim-synthetic-boundary-comparison** (construction, [source](#stmt-boundary-synthetic-trace)): Fix finitely many high and low boundary arcs, separated by transition neighborhoods of positive length, with both types present. The high cores and all their transition neighborhoods lie where the usable actual trace is at least zero; the remaining usable trace is at least $-2$. One may also add real separator pieces, each connected piece meeting its low part and staying a positive distance from the high cores and their transition neighborhoods. There may be arbitrarily many such pieces, for example when two site circuits enter and leave the domain many times. For all sufficiently small meshes there is a synthetic height $K$, obtained from a free ambient spin law by first-color pins and at most $M$ second-color labels, such that its connected prescribed skeleton $S$ has trace $$K\|_{S^+}\in\{-1,0\},\qquad K\|_{S^-}\in\{-3,-2\}. \label{boundary:synthetic-pairs}$$ Here $S=S^+\cup S^-$, the high part contains the high cores and stays inside their prescribed larger arcs, and $M$ depends only on the number of these arcs. It does not depend on the separator pieces, the length of the discrete walk or the number of its repeated vertices. Given its full trace, $K$ has the usual height Gibbs laws in the bounded faces of $S$, and these laws are below the actual laws in height order. Before imposing the second-color labels, an event measurable in the first color and its statuses whose failure probability is $\varepsilon$ has failure probability at most $2^M\varepsilon$ after they are imposed.
  - Explanation: Connected high and low boundary parts and boundedly many complementary labels fix an actual synthetic integer trace below the usable trace, even with many separator pieces.
- **claim-extremal-site-circuit-selection** (construction, [source](#stmt-boundary-extremal)): In a specified finite annular strip, consider the simple open site circuits surrounding a fixed connected inner box. If one exists, there is an innermost and an outermost such circuit, ordered by their geometric Jordan interiors. Selection of the innermost circuit requires only its trace and observations on its inner side in the strip; selection of the outermost requires only its trace and observations on its outer side. Artificial openness as in <a href="#boundary:artificial-exterior" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="boundary:artificial-exterior">[boundary:artificial-exterior]</a> does not change these assertions.* *Consequently, inner circuits selected from the inside and outer circuits selected from the outside in disjoint strips leave the pairwise disjoint unexamined middle components with their height Gibbs laws, independent given the revealed data and their real traces.
  - Explanation: Inner and outer cycle envelopes give extremal circuits whose selection observes only the discarded side, preserving conditional Gibbs laws in unexamined components.
- **claim-clean-boundary-attachment** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-boundary-attachment)): There are constants $\lambda>0$ and $a_0>0$, depending only on $x$, with the following property. Fix $b>0$ and put $s=\lambda b$. Suppose a retained height problem has a connected bounding skeleton consisting of $S_{0,\delta}$ and separator pieces, all with usable trace at least $-2$. A clean local patch of the base skeleton has trace at least zero. Use tangential and inward-normal coordinates $(t,y)$ at this patch, and call $y$ its depth. Assume that all its base-skeleton sites in the box $\|t\|\le 2b$, $\|y\|\le b$ lie in $\|y\|<s/10$, the added separators miss the box, and the compact part above that band is in the domain. The high core and all transition sites can be chosen within $\|t\|<b/3$, with a core covering $\|t\|\le b/8$.* *At all sufficiently small meshes, uniformly in the retained trace, the probability of an actual path of heights at least zero from the clean base patch to depth $s$, staying in $\|t\|<b$, is at least $a_0$. Its boundary endpoint can be joined, through real nonnegative boundary sites in a slightly larger clean patch, to the artificially open exterior.
  - Explanation: A synthetic mean near the clean arc, stopped level-path ceilings, and low lateral barriers force a real nonnegative attachment with fixed positive probability.
- **claim-bulk-nonnegative-tube-network** (bound, [source](#stmt-boundary-bulk-tubes)): Consider a bounded face of a connected fixed skeleton, with its weighted height law and usable trace at least $-2$. Fix a finite network of tubes in that face with positive widths and clearance from the skeleton. Their lengths, widths and clearances are specified by fixed ratios. For all sufficiently small meshes, the probability that every requested tube is traversed in its prescribed direction by a site path of heights at least zero is bounded below by a positive constant depending only on $x$ and the network geometry. The bound is uniform over the shape of the skeleton outside these clearances and over its prescribed trace.
  - Explanation: Flat lower comparison, alternating circuits, and independent loop orientations create nonnegative surrounding paths, which association joins along the tube network.
- **claim-many-scale-boundary-arch** (bound, [source](#stmt-prop-boundary-arch)): There are constants $L>100$, $c,C>0$ and a positive slope tolerance such that the following holds. Fix $p\in\partial D$ and a local radius $R$ satisfying that tolerance. Suppose the actual prescribed trace on $S_{0,\delta}$ is at least $-1$ everywhere and at least zero in $Q_R(p)\setminus Q_r(p)$. Choose any $N$ positive scales $$16r\le\ell_1,\qquad L\ell_j\le\ell_{j+1},\qquad \ell_N\le R/10.$$ At all sufficiently small meshes, $$\mathbb P\!\left( \begin{array}{c} \text{a site circuit in }\widehat{\mathcal O}_0(H) \text{ surrounds }Q_r(p)\\[-2pt] \text{and is contained in }Q_R(p)\setminus Q_r(p) \end{array}\right) \ge 1-Ce^{-cN}. \label{boundary:arch-estimate}$$ The constants are independent of $N,p$ and the prescribed trace; the required mesh threshold may depend on the chosen positive scales and the boundary approximation. The same assertion holds with all inequalities reversed when the original trace is at most $1$ everywhere and at most zero in the clean annulus. All usable sites of the resulting arch have their real height at least zero, or at most zero in the reversed assertion.
  - Explanation: Many preliminary blocks retain independent middle Gibbs problems; uniformly probable attachments and bulk paths upgrade one block to a genuine boundary arch.
- **claim-vanishing-bracket-means** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prop-bracket-collapse)): Fix a finite regular grid as in Definition <a href="#def:brackets" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:brackets">35</a>. For every $f\in C_c^\infty(D)$, the upper and lower bracket fields satisfy $$\lim_{\epsilon\downarrow0}\ \limsup_{\delta\downarrow0} \left\|\mathbb EH_\delta^{\pm,\epsilon}(f)\right\|=0. \label{boundary:bracket-means}$$
  - Explanation: Increasing and decreasing arches screen exceptional windows. Unconditional moment bounds control failed searches and make bracket means vanish in the stated iterated limit.
- **claim-boundary-depth-moments** (bound, [source](#stmt-prop-boundary-moments)): Fix a nonnegative smooth radial bump $\rho$, supported in the unit disk, with integral one, and fix a sufficiently small $\theta>0$. For $z\in D$ write $d(z)=\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}(z,\partial D)$ and $$\rho_z(u)=(\theta d(z))^{-2} \rho\!\left(\frac{u-z}{\theta d(z)}\right),\qquad Y_z=H(\rho_z),$$ where $H$ is any subsequential distributional and moment limit of the true fields. For every $1\le p<\infty$, $$\sup_{z\in D}\\|Y_z\\|_p\le C_{p,\theta,D,\rho}. \label{boundary:uniform-depth-moments}$$ In particular this bound is uniform when $z$ approaches any point of a fixed compact boundary arc.* *Let $p_0\in\partial D$ and let $F$ be a product of a fixed number of smooth averages supported a positive distance from $p_0$. The averages may be fixed in the interior, or may be of the same comparable-depth form with centers approaching fixed boundary points distinct from $p_0$. Then, jointly in those allowed approaches, $$\mathbb E[Y_zF]\longrightarrow0\qquad(z\longrightarrow p_0). \label{boundary:spectator-vanishing}$$ The same statement holds for finite linear combinations of these products.* *If $p_1,\ldots,p_m$ are distinct fixed boundary points and $z_i\to p_i$, then the reference average $Z_m=m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^mY_{z_i}$ satisfies $$\limsup_{z_i\to p_i}\\|Z_m\\|_2\le C m^{-1/2}, \qquad \sup_m\sup_{z_1,\ldots,z_m}\\|Z_m\\|_p\le C_p. \label{boundary:reference-average}$$ In the first assertion $m$ and its distinct boundary points are fixed before taking the depth limits. Subsequently $m\to\infty$ makes these references tend to zero in every finite $L^p$.
  - Explanation: Comparable-depth averages have bounded moments and vanish against distant spectators in boundary limits. Distinct boundary references can then average to zero.
- **claim-local-distribution-tightness** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prop-tightness)): For every $t>1$, the true fields are tight in $H^{-t}_{\mathrm{loc}}(D)$. The same holds for the upper and lower brackets, uniformly in their exceptional windows. Every fixed finite collection of test pairings has uniformly bounded moments of every order. Along a distributional law limit, all its mixed moments converge. These assertions hold also for finite joint couplings of the indicated fields.
  - Explanation: Uniform pairing moments control localized negative Sobolev norms and yield tightness. Uniform integrability transfers every mixed moment along law limits.
- **claim-true-limit-insertion-transfer** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-limit-transfer)): The field $H$ satisfies the limiting insertion identity of Proposition <a href="#prop:bracket-insertion" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:bracket-insertion">44</a> in every disk arrangement allowed there: $$\mathbb E\left[H(\Delta\varphi) \prod_{\ell=1}^k H(g_\ell)\right]=0, \qquad \int g_\ell=0, \label{eq:limit-insertion}$$ where each $g_\ell$ is supported in its indicated spectator disk. The same assertion first holds with each spectator replaced by a bounded continuous function of finitely many zero-total tests in that disk.
  - Explanation: Ordered brackets collapse onto the chosen true-field limit, transferring bounded insertion identities and then their polynomial versions.
- **claim-vanishing-boundary-references** (construction, [source](#stmt-limit-references)): There are finite averages $R_m$ of unit radial pairings of $H$, supported arbitrarily near the boundary, such that $$\\|R_m\\|_{L^p}\longrightarrow0 \quad\text{for every }p<\infty.$$ Each $R_m$ uses finitely many distinct boundary points, with depth chosen after those points are fixed. Its constituent disks can be required to have any prescribed small positive maximum diameter.
  - Explanation: Finite averages at distinct boundary points have vanishing second moments after taking depth limits; interpolation gives convergence in every finite moment norm.
- **claim-separately-harmonic-moments** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prop-harmonic-moments)): Let $$\mathcal C_j=\{(z_1,\ldots,z_j)\in D^j: z_i\ne z_k\text{ for }i\ne k\}.$$ On $\mathcal C_j$, $T_j$ is a smooth function and is harmonic in each variable separately.
  - Explanation: Vanishing boundary references convert arbitrary spectators into sums of local zero-total tests. Insertion identities give separate harmonicity and elliptic regularity off collisions.
- **claim-no-collision-supported-distributions** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-no-diagonal)): On every compact subset of $D^j$, the off-diagonal function from Proposition <a href="#prop:harmonic-moments" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:harmonic-moments">55</a> is locally integrable and represents all of $T_j$. For $j\ge2$, if $d(\mathbf z)=\min_{i<k}\|z_i-z_k\|$, then, locally away from the boundary, $$\|T_j(\mathbf z)\| \le C\bigl(1+\log_+(1/d(\mathbf z))\bigr)^{j/2}, \qquad \mathbf z\in\mathcal C_j. \label{eq:limit-log-bound}$$ Moreover, for distinct fixed $z_2,\ldots,z_j\in D$, $$T_j(z_1,z_2,\ldots,z_j)\longrightarrow0 \quad\text{as }z_1\longrightarrow p\in\partial D. \label{eq:limit-zero-boundary}$$
  - Explanation: Logarithmic mollifier bounds make the collision-tube mass vanish, so the off-diagonal harmonic function represents the complete moment distribution and has zero boundary limits.
- **claim-punctured-logarithmic-expansion** (classification, [source](#stmt-limit-puncture)): Let $j\ge2$. Fix a collision point $y\in D$ and distinct spectators $\mathbf z=(z_3,\ldots,z_j)$, all separated from $y$. For $x$ in a sufficiently small punctured disk about $y$, $$T_j(x,y,\mathbf z) =L(y,\mathbf z)\log(1/\|x-y\|) +R(x;y,\mathbf z), \label{eq:limit-puncture}$$ where $R$ extends harmonically across $x=y$. The coefficient $L$ is smooth in the separated parameters $(y,\mathbf z)$, and the first-variable derivatives of $R$ are bounded uniformly on smaller disks and compact sets of these parameters. The coefficient $L$ is separately harmonic in each spectator variable.
  - Explanation: Logarithmic growth excludes negative angular powers, leaving a logarithmic singularity and a harmonic remainder; flux identifies a smooth spectator-harmonic coefficient.
- **claim-plane-determined-collision-coefficient** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prop-collision)): In <a href="#eq:limit-puncture" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:limit-puncture">[eq:limit-puncture]</a>, $$L(y,\mathbf z)=\frac{v}{2\pi}T_{j-2}(\mathbf z). \label{eq:limit-collision}$$ The convention $T_0=1$ applies when $j=2$.
  - Explanation: A plane increment copy independent of absolute-height spectators fixes the logarithmic coefficient by comparison with the punctured harmonic expansion.
- **claim-wick-full-field-identification** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thm-wick)): For every $j\ge2$ and distinct $x,y_2,\ldots,y_j\in D$, $$T_j(x,y_2,\ldots,y_j) =v\sum_{i=2}^j G_D(x,y_i)\, T_{j-2}(y_2,\ldots,\widehat{y_i},\ldots,y_j). \label{eq:limit-wick}$$ Together with $T_0=1$ and $T_1=0$, this identifies every moment distribution with that of $\sqrt v\,\Phi_D$. Every subsequential field limit has that law. Consequently $h_\delta/\sqrt v$ converges to $\Phi_D$ as a random distribution, with joint convergence of every finite collection of smooth compactly supported pairings.
  - Explanation: Subtracting Green singularities leaves a harmonic function with zero boundary values. Its vanishing gives Wick recursion, Gaussian finite-dimensional laws, and the unique full field limit.
- **claim-commuting-unitary-scalar-measures** (construction, [source](#stmt-spectra-unitary)): Let $V_1,\ldots,V_d$ be commuting unitaries on a complex Hilbert space. For vectors $a,b$ there is a unique finite complex measure $\mu_{a,b}$ on the $d$-torus such that $$\int e^{i\mathbf n\cdot\theta}\,\mu_{a,b}(\,\mathrm d\theta) =\langle a,V_1^{n_1}\cdots V_d^{n_d}b\rangle \qquad(\mathbf n\in\mathbb Z^d).$$ The measure $\mu_{a,a}$ is positive, has mass $\\|a\\|^2$, and $\\|\mu_{a,b}\\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le\\|a\\|\\|b\\|$. For Laurent polynomials $P,Q$, $$\mu_{P(V)a,Q(V)b} =\overline{P(e^{i\theta})}Q(e^{i\theta})\mu_{a,b}.$$ If $P_0$ is the orthogonal projection onto the common invariant subspace, then $\mu_{a,b}(\{0\})=\langle P_0a,P_0b\rangle$.
  - Explanation: Positive trigonometric kernels and polarization construct unique scalar covariance measures, their variation bound, polynomial covariance identity, and invariant atom.
- **claim-positive-transfer-scalar-measures** (construction, [source](#stmt-spectra-transfer)): Let $U$ be unitary and $S$ a positive self-adjoint contraction, with $US=SU$. For vectors $a,b$ there is a unique finite complex measure $\gamma_{a,b}$ on the circle times $[0,1]$ satisfying $$\int e^{im\theta}\lambda^j\,\gamma_{a,b}(\,\mathrm d\theta,\,\mathrm d\lambda) =\langle a,U^mS^jb\rangle \qquad(m\in\mathbb Z,\ j\ge0).$$ The diagonal measures are positive, both endpoint atoms are retained, and $\\|\gamma_{a,b}\\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le\\|a\\|\\|b\\|$.
  - Explanation: Positive Bernstein operator weights construct a joint scalar measure for commuting unitary and positive contraction powers without removing endpoint atoms.
- **claim-holomorphic-positive-power-elements** (construction, [source](#stmt-spectra-analytic)): For the positive contraction $S$ above and vectors $a,b$, there is a bounded holomorphic function $F_{a,b}$ on $\Re w>0$ such that $$F_{a,b}(j)=\langle a,S^jb\rangle\quad(j=1,2,\ldots), \qquad \|F_{a,b}(w)\|\le\\|a\\|\\|b\\|.$$ It is obtained by integrating $\lambda^w$ against the $[0,1]$ marginal of $\gamma_{a,b}$, with value zero at $\lambda=0$.
  - Explanation: Integrating positive complex powers against the finite scalar measure gives a bounded holomorphic interpolation, with no assertion at exponent zero.
- **claim-spherical-ambient-cylinder-law** (construction, [source](#stmt-annulus-ambient)): Take a finite triangulation of the sphere containing a periodic triangular lattice cylinder. Choose any edge-disjoint family of elementary triangles in that cylinder, make each a cell of parameter $q=x^2$, and make each remaining edge a cell of parameter $x$, or of parameter $1$ on a specified set of edges. Use coherent spin pairs and the cell table <a href="#discrete:cell-table" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="discrete:cell-table">[discrete:cell-table]</a>. Proposition <a href="#prop:history-order" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:history-order">6</a> holds for this law, including deterministic $W$-equality edges and its stated first-spin histories. The selected triangles may have either orientation.* *A simple authorized winding contour in the cylindrical portion, with no $W$-equality edge crossing it, has the cut property of Lemma <a href="#lem:cell-cut" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:cell-cut">4</a>. In particular, prescribing a lower open-minus and an upper open-plus contour of class $T$ realizes $P_T$ between those contours, when they bound the rows-cylinder.
  - Explanation: Triangular face equations on the capped sphere preserve wall factorization, restricted-history order, and the winding cut law for edge-disjoint cells of either orientation.
- **claim-one-complementary-winding-cut** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-annulus-one-white)): The comparison of Lemma <a href="#annulus:ambient" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="annulus:ambient">63</a> for $B$ and signed $B$ statuses remains valid with one prescribed open $W$ winding contour of fixed sign, provided that its cells are disjoint from the selected $B$ cells. Histories still observe no other $W$ labels.
  - Explanation: A prescribed complementary-color open winding can be represented by equalities and a single fair label, preserving first-color order when its cells are disjoint.
- **claim-oriented-boundary-slides** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-annulus-slide)): Let $\mu_{a,b}$ be the law between a lower open-minus $B$ contour $a$ and an upper open-plus $B$ contour $b$. If the contours are ordered from bottom to top as $$a_1<a_0<\operatorname{supp}(A)<b_1<b_0,$$ where $A$ is an increasing $B$ and signed-status event, then $$\label{annulus:slide-cuts} \mu_{a_0,b_0}(A)\le \mu_{a_1,b_1}(A).$$ Old and new contours may use different classes, with edge-disjoint cells. In particular, writing $\tau_d A_T$ for the upward translate by $d$ of an increasing class-$T$ test, for $S,T\in\{Y,Z\}$ we have $$\label{annulus:slide-tests} P_S(A_T)\le P_T(\tau_d A_T),$$ whenever the downward-translated class-$T$ boundary contours have the required clearance from the original class-$S$ contours and the test.* *Above a fixed open $W$ contour $\gamma$, let $\nu_{\gamma,b}$ denote the law with upper open-plus $B$ contour $b$. For $\gamma<\operatorname{supp}(A)<b_0<b_1$, the reverse slide gives $$\label{annulus:slide-white} \nu_{\gamma,b_1}(A)\le\nu_{\gamma,b_0}(A).$$
  - Explanation: Moving the adverse lower cut downward and the favorable upper cut downward increases an intervening increasing event. Above a complementary cut, moving the upper favorable cut farther away decreases it.
- **claim-stopped-cylinder-winding-search** (construction, [source](#stmt-annulus-search)): In a cylindrical band, search from below for an authorized winding contour of a specified class, color, and sign. The search can be arranged so that, conditional on each successful complete record, the law above the selected contour is the corresponding cut law. Existence of a winding with fixed clearance inside the search band implies success.
  - Explanation: Authorized-edge invasion from below finds a winding while observing only the discarded side and the prescribed cut layer, leaving the corresponding law above it.
- **claim-signed-cylinder-duality** (classification, [source](#stmt-annulus-duality)): In a cylindrical band augmented in either class $T$, at least one of the following events occurs: a vertical occupied $B+$ crossing, a vertical occupied $B-$ crossing, an occupied $W+$ winding, or an occupied $W-$ winding. Each alternative yields one of a fixed finite family of local horizontal or vertical crossing tests when the band width and circumference are fixed multiples of its height. The number of tests is independent of the lattice scale.
  - Explanation: Joint occupations cover every cell, so absence of a first-color vertical crossing forces a complementary-color winding; their signs yield a finite local test family.
- **claim-finite-port-density-comparison** (bound, [source](#stmt-annulus-ports)): Consider a cell law with no prescribed complementary-spin labels. Suppose that, after a first-spin/status history is fixed outside a retained set, every complementary-spin connection to the exterior passes through at most $K$ sites. The retained cell factors, first-spin pins, and equality constraints are kept fixed. Removing the exterior connections changes the marginal density of the retained $(B,\tau)$ variables by a factor between $2^{-(K-1)_+}$ and $2^{(K-1)_+}$.
  - Explanation: Exterior complementary wiring can merge only boundedly many retained components, giving multiplicative bounds for the normalized first-spin/status density.
- **claim-compatible-local-patch-probability** (bound, [source](#stmt-annulus-patch)): Fix $x$ and a bound $M$ on the number of cells and sites of a patch. Keep the first-spin/status history outside the patch fixed, and reveal no complementary-spin labels. Let $A$ be prescriptions in the patch with the following property: for every feasible exterior configuration, its first spins extend to the patch satisfying $A$ and all common pins, with every prescribed open cell constant of its specified sign and every prescribed closed cell either mixed or of positive weight $1-q_y$. Assume that all cells incident to a mutable patch site are included in the patch. Then $$\mathbb P(A\mid\hbox{exterior }(B,\tau))\geq c(x,M)>0.$$ Consequently conditioning on $A$ changes the probability of any event measurable off the patch by bounded factors depending only on $x,M$.
  - Explanation: Compatible first-spin extensions with a constant complementary label have positive local weight, giving a uniform patch probability and bounded effects on exterior events.
- **claim-equalities-on-plus-layer-order** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-annulus-plus-equalities)): In the law of Lemma <a href="#annulus:ambient" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="annulus:ambient">63</a>, fix a permitted history and an equality set $E_0$. Let $F$ be a set of edges both of whose endpoints are pinned $B=+$. Adding the equalities $W_u=W_v$ for $uv\in F$ stochastically decreases the joint law of $B$ and signed $B$ statuses. There is no restriction on the number of edges in $F$.
  - Explanation: Deleting complementary wall coordinates on edges with both endpoints pinned plus lowers the first-spin and signed-status law; the assertion specifically requires plus pins.
- **claim-straight-short-crossing** (bound, [source](#stmt-annulus-straight-short)): Fix a cell class $T$ and $0<\eta<1/2$. In triangular coordinates let $P=[0,3r]\times[0,r]$. Give its long sides open-plus $B$ cuts and its short sides open-minus $B$ cuts, exclude their boundary-cell factors, and leave complementary-spin labels unobserved. Use feasible bounded transition patches at the four corners. There is $c=c(x,\eta)>0$, independent of $r$, such that, for all sufficiently large $r$, an occupied-plus $T$-site path in $P$ crosses from height $\eta r$ to height $(1-\eta)r$ with probability at least $c$.
  - Explanation: Alternating open boundary arcs, reflection, interface exploration, and bounded complementary wiring give a positive short-direction occupied crossing probability.
- **claim-separated-extremal-path-gluing** (bound, [source](#stmt-annulus-gluing)): Use triangular coordinates $(u,v)$, with $u$ horizontal, and a fixed cell class $T$. Let $$P_L=[0,6\ell]\times[0,\ell],\qquad P_R=[\ell,7\ell]\times[0,\ell]$$ be embedded parallelograms in a matching mixed cylinder. Let $\Gamma_L$ be the uppermost occupied-plus horizontal crossing of $P_L$ and $\Gamma_R$ the lowermost one of $P_R$. Suppose that $\Gamma_L$ lies above $3\ell/4$ and $\Gamma_R$ below $\ell/4$. For all sufficiently large $\ell$ there is $c=c(x)>0$, uniform in the feasible extremal pair and in $\ell$, such that, conditional on this pair, with probability at least $c$ there is an occupied-plus vertical crossing between heights $3\ell/10$ and $7\ell/10$ in the horizontal window $[5\ell/4,23\ell/4]$. The cylinder and lattice rounding are required to leave a fixed-width collar around the displayed parallelograms.
  - Explanation: Exterior records of the full separated paths leave an unobserved stepped region. Compatible patches, port comparison, and the straight crossing bound yield a conditional central connector.
- **claim-seed-in-matching-cell-class** (bound, [source](#stmt-annulus-first-seed)): There is $c=c(x,C)>0$ such that, for each sufficiently large $n$, one of $T=Y,Z$ has a seed of occupied $B$-plus cells, under the matching mixed law $P_T$, in a band of height comparable to $m$ centered near $.71H$. The seed is a horizontal crossing of aspect ratio four or a vertical crossing of aspect ratio six. The choice of class and test may depend on $n$; the lower bound $c$ does not.
  - Explanation: Signed band duality, boundary slides, reflection, and color exchange produce a positively probable seed in one matching cell class without identifying the two class laws.
- **claim-matching-seed-winding** (construction, [source](#stmt-annulus-winding)): Under $P_Z$, the horizontal seed above implies a positive lower bound for an occupied $B$-plus winding of class $Z$ in a thin neighborhood of height $.71H$, entirely below $.73H$. The bound is uniform in $n$.
  - Explanation: Conditional gluing creates seam connectors; lengthened occupied horizontal paths then join a path to its periodic translate and yield a winding cut.
- **claim-requested-cylinder-seed** (bound, [source](#stmt-annulus-seed)): For every fixed $C\geq3$ there is $\delta=\delta(x,C)>0$ such that, for all sufficiently large $n$, $$\label{annulus:seed-bound} P_Y\bigl(\mathsf H_Y^+([-2n,2n]\times[3n,4n])\bigr)\geq\delta$$ on the mixed cylinder $\mathrm{Cyl}_{Cn,5n}$ of (Glazman and Lammers 2025, Appendix A) [[GL2025](#ref-GL2025)], with the same lattice rounding convention.
  - Explanation: A winding in the opposite class screens a fresh requested-class seed; boundary slides and lengthening recover the specified mixed-cylinder crossing.

        "anchor": "stmt-lem-buffer-circuits",
        "exact_quote": "Fix a finite collection of annuli and tubes in a bounded planar region, each with a positive-width buffer and with prescribed geometric clearance. At mesh $\\delta$, suppose the buffers contain no equality edge $E_0$ and no first-spin pin adverse to a requested sign. Then each request for good circuits, or connected good paths formed from a finite annular chain, has probability bounded below by a positive constant independent of $\\delta$ for all sufficiently small $\\delta$. The bound is uniform over feasible histories supported away from the buffers and over lattice translations preserving the clearances. Requests with the same sign may be combined by association; requests of different signs in disjoint buffers may be made successively. In an annular stack of fixed-ratio, separated slots between lattice scales $r$ and $L$, the probability of finding no requested good circuit is at most $$\\label{discrete:stack}\n C(r/L)^\\alpha,$$ for constants $C,\\alpha>0$.*\n\n*Moreover, conditioning a free ambient law on any deterministic collection of open-plus cells and their first-spin values increases every increasing event in $(B,\\tau)$. This applies to a favorable path event in the ambient plane even when its path leaves the interior of a prescribed good contour.",

        "anchor": "stmt-prop-local-mixing",
        "exact_quote": "There are $C,\\alpha>0$ with the following property. Suppose a finite ambient graph contains a ball of radius $L$ together with its interaction cells, and its law has first-spin pins and second-spin equalities, none in that ball. Then its pair marginal in the concentric radius-$r$ ball is within $C(r/L)^\\alpha$ in total variation of a common free plane law, for $L\\ge Cr\\ge C$. The same is true with the statuses of either fixed choice of first color. The plane law is the local limit of free ambient laws along every exhaustion, and its unaugmented pair and increment laws preserve translations, lattice symmetries, and height symmetries.*\n\n*Adding extreme first-spin pins in a bounded inner region can be coupled to the original law so that the configurations agree beyond a common circuit of the added sign. If there are $k$ separated favorable annular slots outside all the changes and no adverse pins or equality edges in their buffers, the failure probability is at most $Ce^{-ck}$. All matches preserve the individual conditional marginals at every joint record as in Lemma <a href=\"#discrete:online\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"discrete:online\">9</a>.",

        "anchor": "stmt-lem-collar-switch",
        "exact_quote": "Suppose two nested good circuits have opposite first-spin signs. Between and on the two circuits assume there are no second-spin equality constraints or prescribed second-spin labels. Conditional on the first spins and cell statuses, there is a deterministically selectable second-spin component in that collar whose fair label flip changes the integer lift throughout the protected inner region by $+4$ or $-4$ relative to the protected exterior, while preserving both spins in both protected regions. The selection uses only the first spins, statuses, equality edges, and the two circuits. It therefore preserves any stopped selection of the circuits based on these data.*\n\n*For disjoint collars the switches commute and give equally weighted orbits containing every parity vector of the corresponding inner lift offsets in $4\\mathbb Z$. Spin constraints and comparisons of lifts along paths inside the protected regions are preserved. With the height anchor fixed in the protected exterior, a test supported there is unchanged; a zero-total test supported entirely in the protected inner region is also unchanged.         "exact_quote": "Let the free sites be in bounded faces of a connected triangular-lattice skeleton of fixed integer trace. Include all neighbors of free sites up to that trace.       "conclusion": {

        "exact_quote": "There is a constant $v=v(x)\\in(0,\\infty)$, depending only on the fixed weight $x$, such that for every pair of real zero-integral tests $f,g\\in C_c^\\infty(\\mathbb R^2)$, $$\\begin{aligned}\n \\lim_{\\delta\\downarrow0}\\mathbb E[H_\\delta(f)H_\\delta(g)]\n &=\\frac{v}{(2\\pi)^2}\n       \\int_{\\mathbb R^2}\\frac{\\widehat f(p)\\overline{\\widehat g(p)}}{|p|^2}\n                  \\,\\mathrm dp                                      \\label{plane:eq:covariance}\\\\\n &=\\frac{v}{2\\pi}\\iint_{\\mathbb R^2\\times\\mathbb R^2}\n          f(z)\\log\\frac1{|z-w|}\\,g(w)\\,\\mathrm dz\\,\\mathrm dw.              \\notag\n\\end{aligned}$$ The conclusion also holds for zero-integral tests converging in $C_c^\\infty$ with a common compact support.",

        "anchor": "stmt-prop-reflection-transfer",
        "exact_quote": "Let $\\ell$ be any row of lattice sites parallel to one of the three unoriented nearest-neighbor directions, and choose one of its closed half-planes. The plane pair is reflection positive across $\\ell$. The assertion remains valid after adjoining any finite collection of fields $$\\label{plane:eq:phases}\n Z_s(u)=U_s\\exp\\{is(H(u)-H(o))\\},$$ where the $U_s$ are independent unit-circle Haar variables, independent of the pair, and $o$ is any anchor.*\n\n*More precisely, let $\\theta_\\ell$ act on observables by spatial reflection, and take local functions supported in the chosen half-plane, whose height differences are evaluated along paths in that half-plane. Then $$\\langle F,G\\rangle_\\ell\n     =\\mathbb E\\big[\\overline{\\theta_\\ell F}\\,G\\big]$$ is a positive semidefinite Hermitian form. In its quotient completion, translation farther into the half-plane by the pure normal vector of length $\\sqrt3$ is a positive self-adjoint contraction $S$. Unit translation along the row is a commuting unitary $U$. At mesh $\\delta$ the normal step is $\\sqrt3\\delta$.",

        "anchor": "stmt-boundary-synthetic-trace",
        "exact_quote": "Fix finitely many high and low boundary arcs, separated by transition neighborhoods of positive length, with both types present. The high cores and all their transition neighborhoods lie where the usable actual trace is at least zero; the remaining usable trace is at least $-2$. One may also add real separator pieces, each connected piece meeting its low part and staying a positive distance from the high cores and their transition neighborhoods. There may be arbitrarily many such pieces, for example when two site circuits enter and leave the domain many times. For all sufficiently small meshes there is a synthetic height $K$, obtained from a free ambient spin law by first-color pins and at most $M$ second-color labels, such that its connected prescribed skeleton $S$ has trace $$K|_{S^+}\\in\\{-1,0\\},\\qquad\n K|_{S^-}\\in\\{-3,-2\\}.\n \\label{boundary:synthetic-pairs}$$ Here $S=S^+\\cup S^-$, the high part contains the high cores and stays inside their prescribed larger arcs, and $M$ depends only on the number of these arcs. It does not depend on the separator pieces, the length of the discrete walk or the number of its repeated vertices. Given its full trace, $K$ has the usual height Gibbs laws in the bounded faces of $S$, and these laws are below the actual laws in height order. Before imposing the second-color labels, an event measurable in the first color and its statuses whose failure probability is $\\varepsilon$ has failure probability at most $2^M\\varepsilon$ after they are imposed.",

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-lem-boundary-attachment",
        "exact_quote": "There are constants $\\lambda>0$ and $a_0>0$, depending only on $x$, with the following property. Fix $b>0$ and put $s=\\lambda b$. Suppose a retained height problem has a connected bounding skeleton consisting of $S_{0,\\delta}$ and separator pieces, all with usable trace at least $-2$. A clean local patch of the base skeleton has trace at least zero. Use tangential and inward-normal coordinates $(t,y)$ at this patch, and call $y$ its depth. Assume that all its base-skeleton sites in the box $|t|\\le 2b$, $|y|\\le b$ lie in $|y|<s/10$, the added separators miss the box, and the compact part above that band is in the domain. The high core and all transition sites can be chosen within $|t|<b/3$, with a core covering $|t|\\le b/8$.*\n\n*At all sufficiently small meshes, uniformly in the retained trace, the probability of an actual path of heights at least zero from the clean base patch to depth $s$, staying in $|t|<b$, is at least $a_0$. Its boundary endpoint can be joined, through real nonnegative boundary sites in a slightly larger clean patch, to the artificially open exterior.",
        "source_id": "PM-232.1"
      },
      "evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-lem-boundary-attachment",
          "exact_quote": "There are constants $\\lambda>0$ and $a_0>0$, depending only on $x$, with the following property. Fix $b>0$ and put $s=\\lambda b$. A clean local patch of the base skeleton has trace at least zero. Use tangential and inward-normal coordinates $(t,y)$ at this patch, and call $y$ its depth. Assume that all its base-skeleton sites in the box $|t|\\le 2b$, $|y|\\le b$ lie in $|y|<s/10$, the added separators miss the box, and the compact part above that band is in the domain. The high core and all transition sites can be chosen within $|t|<b/3$, with a core covering $|t|\\le b/8$.*\n\n*At all sufficiently small meshes, uniformly in the retained trace, the probability of an actual path of heights at least zero from the clean base patch to depth $s$, staying in $|t|<b$, is at least $a_0$.         "exact_quote": "There are constants $L>100$, $c,C>0$ and a positive slope tolerance such that the following holds. Fix $p\\in\\partial D$ and a local radius $R$ satisfying that tolerance. The same assertion holds with all inequalities reversed when the original trace is at most $1$ everywhere and at most zero in the clean annulus.         "anchor": "stmt-prop-boundary-moments",
        "exact_quote": "Fix a nonnegative smooth radial bump $\\rho$, supported in the unit disk, with integral one, and fix a sufficiently small $\\theta>0$. For $z\\in D$ write $d(z)=\\mathop{\\mathrm{dist}}(z,\\partial D)$ and $$\\rho_z(u)=(\\theta d(z))^{-2}\n       \\rho\\!\\left(\\frac{u-z}{\\theta d(z)}\\right),\\qquad\n Y_z=H(\\rho_z),$$ where $H$ is any subsequential distributional and moment limit of the true fields. For every $1\\le p<\\infty$, $$\\sup_{z\\in D}\\|Y_z\\|_p\\le C_{p,\\theta,D,\\rho}.\n \\label{boundary:uniform-depth-moments}$$ In particular this bound is uniform when $z$ approaches any point of a fixed compact boundary arc.*\n\n\n*Let $p_0\\in\\partial D$ and let $F$ be a product of a fixed number of smooth averages supported a positive distance from $p_0$. The averages may be fixed in the interior, or may be of the same comparable-depth form with centers approaching fixed boundary points distinct from $p_0$. Then, jointly in those allowed approaches, $$\\mathbb E[Y_zF]\\longrightarrow0\\qquad(z\\longrightarrow p_0).\n \\label{boundary:spectator-vanishing}$$ The same statement holds for finite linear combinations of these products.*\n\n\n*If $p_1,\\ldots,p_m$ are distinct fixed boundary points and $z_i\\to p_i$, then the reference average $Z_m=m^{-1}\\sum_{i=1}^mY_{z_i}$ satisfies $$\\limsup_{z_i\\to p_i}\\|Z_m\\|_2\\le C m^{-1/2},\n \\qquad \\sup_m\\sup_{z_1,\\ldots,z_m}\\|Z_m\\|_p\\le C_p.\n \\label{boundary:reference-average}$$ In the first assertion $m$ and its distinct boundary points are fixed before taking the depth limits.         "exact_quote": "Take a finite triangulation of the sphere containing a periodic triangular lattice cylinder.
