<a id="pm-s2"></a>
## 2. Definitions, validity and bounds

- **Inside approximation** ([source](#stmt-def-approximation)): Let $D\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a bounded simply connected domain with $C^2$ Jordan boundary. For each mesh $\delta$ in a sequence tending to zero, let $\gamma_\delta$ be a simple cycle in $\delta\mathbb H$, let $D_\delta$ be its bounded interior, and include every lattice vertex and edge on or inside the cycle. We require $D_\delta\subset D$, that every compact subset of $D$ is eventually contained in $D_\delta$, and that there are parametrizations $$\gamma_\delta:S^1\longrightarrow\partial D_\delta, \qquad \gamma:S^1\longrightarrow\partial D, \qquad \\|\gamma_\delta-\gamma\\|_\infty\longrightarrow0.$$ Here each parametrization is a homeomorphism onto the indicated curve. Write $F_\delta$ for the hexagonal faces enclosed by $\gamma_\delta$, and $\partial F_\delta$ for those adjacent to the boundary cycle.
- **Weighted integer Lipschitz height law** ([source](#eq:model)): Fix $x\in[1/\sqrt2,1]$. An admissible height is a function $h:F_\delta\to\mathbb Z$ such that $$h=0\quad\text{on }\partial F_\delta, \qquad \|h(u)-h(v)\|\le1\quad\text{whenever }u\sim v.$$ Its probability is $$\label{eq:model} \mathbb P_{\delta,x}(h)=\frac{x^{N_\delta(h)}}{Z_{\delta,x}}, \qquad N_\delta(h)=\sum_{\{u,v\}\subset F_\delta:\,u\sim v} \mathbf 1_{\{h(u)\ne h(v)\}}.$$ The sum counts each unordered adjacent pair once. The admissible set is finite, since the height at any face is bounded in absolute value by its graph distance to $\partial F_\delta$. It contains the zero function, so $Z_{\delta,x}$ is finite and positive. Height reflection preserves <a href="#eq:model" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:model">[eq:model]</a>; in particular, $\mathbb Eh_\delta(u)=0$.
- **Euclidean area pairing** ([source](#eq:area-pairing)): $$\label{eq:area-pairing} h_\delta(f)=\int_D h_\delta(z)f(z)\,\mathrm dz =\sum_{u\in F_\delta} w_{\delta,f}(u)h_\delta(u), \qquad w_{\delta,f}(u)=\int_{\text{face at }u}f(z)\,\mathrm dz.$$ For small enough $\delta$, these weights sum to $\int_D f$ exactly.
- **Zero-Dirichlet Gaussian free field covariance** ([source](#eq:gff-covariance)): $$\label{eq:gff-covariance} \mathbb E[\Phi_D(f)\Phi_D(g)] =\iint_{D\times D} f(z)G_D(z,w)g(w)\,\mathrm dz\,\mathrm dw, \qquad G_D=(-\Delta_D)^{-1}.$$ The Laplacian is the Euclidean Laplacian. Thus the singular part of $G_D(z,w)$ is $(2\pi)^{-1}\log(1/\|z-w\|)$.
- **Coherent spin pair** ([source](#discrete:gray)): Call a spin pair coherent if on each edge at least one of its two spins is constant.
- **Signed open-cell status** ([source](#discrete:cell-table)): An open cell is denoted $+$ or $-$ according to its constant $B$ value, and a closed cell is denoted $0$; thus $\tau_y\in\{-,0,+\}$.
- **Restricted history** ([source](#pm-h-13)): A *history* fixes some first-spin sites and some cell statuses, with the rule that it fixes *all* first-spin sites of every observed cell.
- **Smearing** ([source](#moments:weights)): A *smearing of radius $a\geq1$ and weight bound $A$* is a linear statistic $$\label{moments:weights} Y(H)=\sum_u w_uH(u),\qquad \mathop{\mathrm{supp}}w\subset B(z_0,a),\qquad \sum_u\|w_u\|\leq A,\qquad \sup_u\|w_u\|\leq Aa^{-2}.$$
- **Zero-total smearing** ([source](#moments:weights)): If $\sum_uw_u=0$, we call the smearing *zero-total*; its value is independent of the additive constant in the height lift.
- **Rounded midpoint maps** ([source](#stmt-thm-midpoint)): Let $f,g,u,v:\mathbb Z^m\longrightarrow[0,\infty)$ have finite support, and write $m_-(s,t)=\lfloor(s+t)/2\rfloor$ and $m_+(s,t)=\lceil(s+t)/2\rceil$, with coordinatewise rounding.
- **Periodic Cauchy kernels** ([source](#plane:eq:cauchy)): $$\label{plane:eq:cauchy} Q_s(\,\mathrm dl)=q_s(l)\,\mathrm dl,\qquad q_s(l)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z}\frac{s}{\pi\{s^2+(l+nP)^2\}}.$$ Here and below an integral over $l$ uses the centered period. Set $Q_0=\delta_0$ and let $Q_\infty$ be uniform probability on that circle.
- **Filled brackets** ([source](#stmt-def-brackets)): In the plane spin law impose $B=+$ on all of $S_{0,\delta}$ and $W=+$ on $A_{\delta,\epsilon}$. Anchor the height to zero at one doubly pinned vertex, and restrict it to the original interior. Its law is the *upper filled bracket*, denoted $H_\delta^{+,\epsilon}$. For the *lower filled bracket* $H_\delta^{-,\epsilon}$ interchange the colors: impose $W=+$ on the whole skeleton and $B=+$ on $A_{\delta,\epsilon}$, with the same zero anchor.
- **Checked local pin event** ([source](#pins:checked-event)): $$\label{pins:checked-event} P_{\mathrm{loc}}=P\cap\bigcap_{i=1}^m C_i.$$ The checks are not included in the probabilities $p_{i,\delta}$.
- **Haar-lift phases** ([source](#pins:haar-phase)): $$\label{pins:haar-phase} Z_\theta(v)=U_\theta\exp\{i\theta(H(v)-H(o))\},$$ with an independent uniform unit complex variable for every phase field needed. Two factors from the same field share this auxiliary variable, so $Z_\theta(v)\overline{Z_\theta(w)} =\exp\{i\theta(H(v)-H(w))\}$. Changing the anchor is absorbed by Haar invariance. The joint spin, increment, and phase law is reflection positive, and a phase value at a site on one side of a row belongs to that side’s algebra. Thus each factor can move with its own obstacle, including when its balancing factor lies on the other side of the row.
- **Common-offset event** ([source](#pins:common-offset-event)): $$\label{pins:common-offset-event} P_= =P_{\mathrm{loc}}\cap\{D_i=0\text{ for all }i\ge2\}.$$ Fourier orthogonality on the integer variables gives $$\label{pins:fourier-projection} \mathbf 1_{P_=}= \frac{\mathbf 1_{P_{\mathrm{loc}}}}{(2\pi)^{m-1}} \int_{[0,2\pi]^{m-1}} \exp\left(i\sum_{i=2}^m s_iD_i\right)\,\,\mathrm ds.$$ For each fixed $s$, Lemma <a href="#pins:three-moves" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="pins:three-moves">42</a> applies to the right-hand character. At this fixed geometry its normalized integrand is bounded uniformly in $s$ and $\delta$, since $$J_\delta^{-1}\mathbb E[\|X_\delta F_\delta\|\mathbf 1_{P_{\mathrm{loc}}}] \le \frac{\mathbb P(P)}{J_\delta}\,C_F \mathbb E[\|X_\delta\|\mid P_{\mathrm{loc}}]\le C.$$ Equations <a href="#pins:multiplicative" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="pins:multiplicative">[pins:multiplicative]</a> and <a href="#eq:pin-moments" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:pin-moments">[eq:pin-moments]</a> justify this bound. Dominated convergence in <a href="#pins:fourier-projection" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="pins:fourier-projection">[pins:fourier-projection]</a> yields $$\label{pins:common-offset-numerator} J_\delta^{-1}\mathbb E[X_\delta F_\delta\mathbf 1_{P_=}] \longrightarrow0.$$
- **Artificial exterior openness** ([source](#boundary:artificial-exterior)): For a height $H$ and a level $t$, put $$\widehat{\mathcal O}_t(H) = (\delta\mathbb T\setminus V_\delta) \,\cup\,\{v\in V_\delta:H(v)\ge t\}. \label{boundary:artificial-exterior}$$ Thus only sites outside the *original* height problem are declared open artificially. A real vertex which is removed during a search is still a real vertex, with its observed height. For the reversed convention replace $H\ge t$ by $H\le t$.

          "anchor": "stmt-prop-local-mixing",
          "exact_quote": "There are $C,\\alpha>0$ with the following property. Suppose a finite ambient graph contains a ball of radius $L$ together with its interaction cells, and its law has first-spin pins and second-spin equalities, none in that ball. Then its pair marginal in the concentric radius-$r$ ball is within $C(r/L)^\\alpha$ in total variation of a common free plane law, for $L\\ge Cr\\ge C$. The same is true with the statuses of either fixed choice of first color. The plane law is the local limit of free ambient laws along every exhaustion, and its unaugmented pair and increment laws preserve translations, lattice symmetries, and height symmetries.*\n\n*Adding extreme first-spin pins in a bounded inner region can be coupled to the original law so that the configurations agree beyond a common circuit of the added sign. If there are $k$ separated favorable annular slots outside all the changes and no adverse pins or equality edges in their buffers, the failure probability is at most $Ce^{-ck}$. All matches preserve the individual conditional marginals at every joint record as in Lemma <a href=\"#discrete:online\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"discrete:online\">9</a>.",
          "source_id": "PM-232.1"
        }

          "exact_quote": "Let $\\ell$ be any row of lattice sites parallel to one of the three unoriented nearest-neighbor directions, and choose one of its closed half-planes. The plane pair is reflection positive across $\\ell$. The assertion remains valid after adjoining any finite collection of fields $$\\label{plane:eq:phases}\n Z_s(u)=U_s\\exp\\{is(H(u)-H(o))\\},$$ where the $U_s$ are independent unit-circle Haar variables, independent of the pair, and $o$ is any anchor.*\n\n*More precisely, let $\\theta_\\ell$ act on observables by spatial reflection, and take local functions supported in the chosen half-plane, whose height differences are evaluated along paths in that half-plane. Then $$\\langle F,G\\rangle_\\ell\n     =\\mathbb E\\big[\\overline{\\theta_\\ell F}\\,G\\big]$$ is a positive semidefinite Hermitian form. In its quotient completion, translation farther into the half-plane by the pure normal vector of length $\\sqrt3$ is a positive self-adjoint contraction $S$. Unit translation along the row is a commuting unitary $U$. At mesh $\\delta$ the normal step is $\\sqrt3\\delta$.",

          "exact_quote": "Now take any sequence along which $C_h\\to c\\,\\mathrm dp/|p|^2$. On a dyadic annulus $R<|p|\\le2R$ with $R>10$, it is supported on $|k|\\le1$. Equation <a href=\"#plane:eq:endcaps\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"plane:eq:endcaps\">[plane:eq:endcaps]</a>, used at physical scales $b=hR$ and horizontal width $h$, bounds that mass by $K/R$. Summing dyadic annuli gives a uniform $O(1/R)$ tail, up to the edge of the fixed support of $Q$. Vague convergence on the remaining compact annulus therefore gives $$\\begin{aligned}\n L&=c\\int_{\\mathbb R^2}\\frac{\\chi(k,l)}{|p|^2}\n              [q_0(|p|)-q_0(k)]\\,\\mathrm dp \\notag\\\\\n  &=c\\int_0^{2\\pi}\\cos(4u)\n       \\int_0^\\infty[q_0(r)-q_0(r|\\cos u|)]\\frac{\\,\\mathrm dr}{r}\\,\\mathrm du\n    =-\\frac\\pi2c.                       \\label{plane:eq:cutoff-value}\n\\end{aligned}$$ For completeness, for $t>0$ the inner radial integral with $t=|\\cos u|$ equals $\\log t$: integrate first from $\\varepsilon$ to $M$, change variables in the second term, then use that $q_0=1$ near zero and vanishes for large argument. Its absolute integral is bounded by $K(1+|\\log t|)$, which is integrable in $u$, justifying Fubini. The angular value can be checked without a Fourier-series limit: $$\\int_0^{2\\pi}\\cos(4u)\\log|\\cos u|\\,\\mathrm du\n =4\\int_0^{\\pi/2}\\cos(4u)\\log(\\cos u)\\,\\mathrm du\n =4\\int_0^{\\pi/2}\\sin^2u\\cos(2u)\\,\\mathrm du\n =-\\frac\\pi2.$$ The middle equality follows by integration by parts; the boundary term $\\sin(4u)\\log(\\cos u)$ vanishes at both ends. Since $L$ was defined by a full limit, <a href=\"#plane:eq:cutoff-value\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"plane:eq:cutoff-value\">[plane:eq:cutoff-value]</a> fixes the same $c$ for every subsequence. ## 3. Proof roadmap

- **step-midpoint-sum-inequality** [claim](#stmt-thm-midpoint) / [proof](#proof-stmt-thm-midpoint): Entropy deduction followed by coordinate induction. -> Rounded-midpoint inequality for total sums.
- **step-integrable-spin-lift** [claim](#stmt-lem-spin-lift) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-spin-lift): Triangle circulation and integration on a triangulated disk. -> Anchored weighted integer lift.
- **step-open-cell-cut** [claim](#stmt-lem-cell-cut) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-cell-cut): Product factorization at open crossing cells. -> Independent retained specifications with ordinary height interiors.
- **step-ising-partition-lattice** [claim](#stmt-discrete-ising-partition) / [proof](#proof-stmt-discrete-ising-partition): Random-cluster covariance and integration of mixed derivatives. -> Monotone log-supermodular partition sums.
- **step-history-order** [claim](#stmt-prop-history-order) / [proof](#proof-stmt-discrete-ising-partition-2): Wall factorization, sorted supports, and ordered status kernels. -> Joint association and conditional stochastic order.
- **step-online-kernels** [claim](#stmt-discrete-online) / [proof](#proof-stmt-discrete-online): Finite recursive block coupling and backward induction. -> Correct conditional marginals at every reached record.
- **step-spherical-extension** [claim](#stmt-annulus-ambient) / [proof](#proof-stmt-annulus-ambient): Sphere triangle equations and edge-disjoint cell factorization. -> Cylinder-compatible order and winding cuts.
- **step-complementary-winding** [claim](#stmt-annulus-one-white) / [proof](#proof-stmt-annulus-one-white): Equality representation and a fair global component label. -> Preserved first-color comparison.
- **step-boundary-slides** [claim](#stmt-annulus-slide) / [proof](#proof-stmt-annulus-slide): Prescribe, release, and discard ordered contour cuts. -> Directional slide inequalities and translated tests.
- **step-cylinder-search** [claim](#stmt-annulus-search) / [proof](#proof-stmt-annulus-search): Exterior authorized-edge face invasion. -> Stopped winding cut with unobserved retained side.
- **step-band-duality** [claim](#stmt-annulus-duality) / [proof](#proof-stmt-annulus-duality): Covering occupations and triangular-site cylinder duality. -> Signed crossing or winding alternatives and local test extraction.
- **step-port-comparison** [claim](#stmt-annulus-ports) / [proof](#proof-stmt-annulus-ports): Count complementary components merged by exterior wiring. -> Two-sided normalized density factors.
- **step-compatible-patches** [claim](#stmt-annulus-patch) / [proof](#proof-stmt-annulus-patch): Positive compatible local extensions and partition-sum comparison. -> Uniform local prescription probability.
- **step-plus-equality-order** [claim](#stmt-annulus-plus-equalities) / [proof](#proof-stmt-annulus-plus-equalities): Delete plus-wall coordinates and compare restored status kernels. -> Stochastic decrease under equality insertion.
- **step-straight-short-crossing** [claim](#stmt-annulus-straight-short) / [proof](#proof-stmt-annulus-straight-short): Interface exploration, reflected domain duality, and boundary wiring comparison. -> Positive short-direction occupied crossing probability.
- **step-separated-path-gluing** [claim](#stmt-annulus-gluing) / [proof](#proof-stmt-annulus-gluing): Stepped-domain comparison retaining full extremal path records. -> Conditional central vertical connector.
- **step-first-matching-seed** [claim](#stmt-annulus-first-seed) / [proof](#proof-stmt-annulus-first-seed): Signed alternatives, reflection, color exchange, and upward test slides. -> Positive seed in one matching cell class.
- **step-seed-winding** [claim](#stmt-annulus-winding) / [proof](#proof-stmt-annulus-winding): Separated-path gluing and seam connections in the flat cover. -> Occupied winding in the opposite cell class.
- **step-requested-seed** [claim](#stmt-annulus-seed) / [proof](#proof-stmt-annulus-seed): Fresh requested-class test above a winding and class-changing boundary slides. -> Specified mixed-cylinder horizontal seed.
- **step-annulus-circuit** [claim](#stmt-thm-circuit-input) / [proof](#proof-stmt-annulus-seed-2): Cited pushing and renormalization implications, then finite-scale feasibility. -> Adverse-boundary annulus circuit estimate.
- **step-buffered-circuits** [claim](#stmt-lem-buffer-circuits) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-buffer-circuits): Filled-disk adverse comparison, intersecting annular chains, and successive slots. -> Uniform circuit/path probabilities and stack failure bound.
- **step-plane-local-matching** [claim](#stmt-prop-local-mixing) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-local-mixing): Ordered inward and outward common-circuit coupling followed by exhaustion. -> Unique symmetric free-plane increment law and local matching.
- **step-record-independent-plane** [claim](#stmt-cor-conditional-plane-matching) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cor-conditional-plane-matching): Recordwise maximal coupling with a fixed second marginal. -> Plane marginal independent of the complete exterior record.
- **step-rare-pin-products** [claim](#stmt-prop-rare-pins) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-rare-pins): Single-sign cut comparisons, equality events, and bounded label costs. -> Multiplicative comparison for rare separated events.
- **step-protected-switch** [claim](#stmt-lem-collar-switch) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-collar-switch): Component potentials and deterministically selected fair-label involutions. -> Commuting protected offset parity switches.
- **step-height-order** [claim](#stmt-lem-height-order) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-height-order): Convex edge sorting and conditionally fair loop orientations. -> Height association, trace comparison, and stopped flat-loop law.
- **step-shell-tail** [claim](#stmt-lem-shell-moments) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-shell-moments): Stopped loop recursion with a uniformly probable wall obstruction. -> Uniform exponential shell-count tails.
- **step-common-loop-covariance** [claim](#stmt-moments-covariance) / [proof](#proof-stmt-moments-covariance): Common-loop identity, annular arm suppression, and layer-cake averaging. -> Logarithmic covariance and smearing second-moment bounds.
- **step-weighted-midpoints** [claim](#stmt-moments-weighted-midpoints) / [proof](#proof-stmt-moments-weighted-midpoints): Nearest integer half-differences and absolute edge-energy comparison. -> Admissible rounded midpoints, weight inequality, and rounding bound.
- **step-class-amplification** [claim](#stmt-lem-midpoint-amplification) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-midpoint-amplification): Dyadic tail intervals and a squared-probability midpoint recursion. -> Exponential statistic tails and all finite moment bounds.
- **step-bounded-smearing** [claim](#stmt-prop-smearing) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-smearing): Chebyshev central mass, midpoint amplification, and flat-trace comparison. -> Shape-uniform finite smearing moments.
- **step-plane-smearing** [claim](#stmt-prop-plane-moments) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-plane-moments): Stopped cut central mass, anchored increment identification, and exhaustion. -> Scale-uniform plane and free-volume moments.
- **step-two-disk-variance** [claim](#stmt-lem-nondegeneracy) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-nondegeneracy): Fair protected switch across nested opposite cuts. -> Strictly positive second-moment lower bound.
- **step-unitary-measures** [claim](#stmt-spectra-unitary) / [proof](#proof-stmt-spectra-unitary): Positive finite trigonometric kernels, compact extraction, and polarization. -> Unique scalar covariance measures and invariant atoms.
- **step-positive-transfer-measures** [claim](#stmt-spectra-transfer) / [proof](#proof-stmt-spectra-transfer): Positive Bernstein operator weights and compact scalar measures. -> Joint scalar measures retaining endpoint atoms.
- **step-analytic-powers** [claim](#stmt-spectra-analytic) / [proof](#proof-stmt-spectra-analytic): Complex positive powers and dominated differentiation. -> Bounded holomorphic matrix elements.
- **step-normal-transfer** [claim](#stmt-prop-reflection-transfer) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-reflection-transfer): Row conditioning, reflected translations, and bounded log-convex norms. -> Reflection space, positive normal contraction, and tangential unitary.
- **step-punctured-spectrum** [claim](#stmt-plane-lem-spectrum) / [proof](#proof-stmt-plane-lem-spectrum): Cocycle patching of scalar measures and zero-total tilt exclusion. -> Symmetric punctured spectrum with annular bounds and no linear tilt.
- **step-cauchy-mixture** [claim](#stmt-plane-lem-mixture) / [proof](#proof-stmt-plane-lem-mixture): Transfer-power Fourier coefficients and rotated exceptional-set tests. -> Positive projected Cauchy mixture and absence of alias atoms.
- **step-summable-defect** [claim](#stmt-plane-lem-defect) / [proof](#proof-stmt-plane-lem-defect): Poisson angular identity, controlled periodization, and rotational cancellation. -> Integrable dispersion defect and bounded mixing bands.
- **step-endcap-control** [claim](#stmt-lem-endcaps) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-endcaps): Rotate caps and bound normal densities away from their atom. -> Quantitative endcap mass control.
- **step-isotropic-spectral-limits** [claim](#stmt-plane-lem-subsequences) / [proof](#proof-stmt-plane-lem-subsequences): Concentrate rescaled mixtures and annihilate independent directional derivatives. -> Inverse-square density for every vague subsequential spectrum.
- **step-unique-spectral-limit** [claim](#stmt-plane-lem-unique) / [proof](#proof-stmt-plane-lem-unique): Full signed-cutoff limit followed by its angular evaluation. -> Unique coefficient and full vague convergence.
- **step-plane-covariance** [claim](#stmt-prop-plane-covariance) / [proof](#proof-stmt-plane-lem-unique-2): Exact area transform convergence, spectral tail bounds, and nondegeneracy. -> Positive domain-independent Green covariance multiplier.
- **step-reflection-null** [claim](#stmt-prop-reflection-null) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-reflection-null): Green covariance for disjoint reflected Laplace tests. -> Vanishing reflection seminorm and bounded ordinary moments.
- **step-boundary-walk** [claim](#stmt-lem-boundary-walk) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-boundary-walk): Incident-face traversal and uniformly convergent boundary parametrizations. -> Separating face-center walk with controlled projected excursions.
- **step-label-count** [claim](#stmt-pins-label-count) / [proof](#proof-stmt-pins-label-count): Charge retained components to disjoint traversal excursions. -> Uniform bound on retained connected component labels.
- **step-bracket-integer-order** [claim](#stmt-pins-bracket-order) / [proof](#proof-stmt-pins-bracket-order): Connected lifted pairs and conditional height trace comparison. -> Actual integer bracket traces and ordered true-field coupling.
- **step-marker-checks** [claim](#stmt-pins-marker-checks) / [proof](#proof-stmt-pins-marker-checks): Favorable circuit stacks joining all marker-crossing chains. -> Asymptotically successful common-pair checks.
- **step-checked-pin-moments** [claim](#stmt-prop-pin-moments) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-pin-moments): Parity partition, protected switch orbits, and classwise midpoint amplification. -> Uniform moments after rare checked conditioning.
- **step-side-norm** [claim](#stmt-pins-side-norm) / [proof](#proof-stmt-pins-side-norm): Double the arrangement by reflection and cancel multiplicative pin factors. -> Bounded normalized reflection norm.
- **step-analytic-motion** [claim](#stmt-lem-analytic-translation) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-analytic-translation): Positive-step backoff, bounded holomorphic compactness, and identity theorem. -> Vanishing at the original placement.
- **step-local-grid** [claim](#stmt-pins-local-geometry) / [proof](#proof-stmt-pins-local-geometry): Regular-level avoidance and oblique projection separation. -> A finite grid usable for each allowed spectator arrangement.
- **step-separated-insertion** [claim](#stmt-pins-three-moves) / [proof](#proof-stmt-pins-three-moves): Outward motion in lattice mirror normals and reverse analytic continuation. -> Normalized checked insertion vanishes.
- **step-gap-closing** [claim](#stmt-pins-gap-closing) / [proof](#proof-stmt-pins-gap-closing): Gap circuit stacks, stopped exterior coupling, and independent common-offset moment amplification. -> Offset synchronization, local increment comparison, and gap-uniform moments.
- **step-bracket-insertion** [claim](#stmt-prop-bracket-insertion) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-bracket-insertion): Balanced character projection, common-offset normalization, and truncation. -> Insertion identity in both filled brackets.
- **step-synthetic-trace** [claim](#stmt-boundary-synthetic-trace) / [proof](#proof-stmt-boundary-synthetic-trace): Connected core growth and labelled spanning-tree transitions. -> Synthetic ordered integer trace with bounded label cost.
- **step-extremal-circuits** [claim](#stmt-boundary-extremal) / [proof](#proof-stmt-boundary-extremal): Inner and outer Jordan envelopes and discarded-side measurability. -> Extremal stopped separators retaining independent Gibbs middle components.
- **step-clean-attachment** [claim](#stmt-lem-boundary-attachment) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-boundary-attachment): Synthetic reflection mean, stopped level-path ceilings, and lateral low barriers. -> Positive probability of a genuine nonnegative boundary attachment.
- **step-bulk-tubes** [claim](#stmt-boundary-bulk-tubes) / [proof](#proof-stmt-boundary-bulk-tubes): Flat lower comparison, fair loop increments, and intersecting annular chains. -> Uniform nonnegative bulk path crossings.
- **step-boundary-arches** [claim](#stmt-prop-boundary-arch) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-boundary-arch): Preliminary block count and independent retained-block upgrades. -> Exponential failure estimate for a level-zero boundary arch.
- **step-bracket-collapse** [claim](#stmt-prop-bracket-collapse) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-bracket-collapse): Innermost increasing and decreasing arches plus unconditional moment bounds. -> Bracket means vanish after mesh and window limits.
- **step-boundary-moments** [claim](#stmt-prop-boundary-moments) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-boundary-moments): Comparable-depth smearings and outermost arches with exterior-measurable spectators. -> Uniform depth moments, vanishing spectator correlations, and small reference averages.
- **step-tightness** [claim](#stmt-prop-tightness) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-tightness): Localized Fourier moments, compact Sobolev inclusion, and uniform integrability. -> Local distribution tightness and convergence of mixed moments.
- **step-limit-insertion** [claim](#stmt-limit-transfer) / [proof](#proof-stmt-limit-transfer): Ordered joint limits, expectation-zero collapse, and polynomial truncation. -> Insertion identity for the chosen true limit.
- **step-vanishing-references** [claim](#stmt-limit-references) / [proof](#proof-stmt-limit-references): Distinct-boundary average decorrelation followed by moment interpolation. -> Finite references converging to zero in all finite moment norms.
- **step-harmonic-moments** [claim](#stmt-prop-harmonic-moments) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-harmonic-moments): Telescoping zero-total test chains, reference removal, and elliptic regularity. -> Smooth separately harmonic off-diagonal moments.
- **step-no-diagonal** [claim](#stmt-lem-no-diagonal) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-no-diagonal): Radial mean values, logarithmic mollifier control, and vanishing collision-tube mass. -> Full locally integrable moment distributions and zero boundary values.
- **step-puncture-expansion** [claim](#stmt-limit-puncture) / [proof](#proof-stmt-limit-puncture): Angular harmonic modes and flux extraction. -> Smooth logarithmic coefficient and removable harmonic remainder.
- **step-collision-coefficient** [claim](#stmt-prop-collision) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-collision): Conditional independent plane matching and a second evaluation of signed local pairings. -> Collision coefficient fixed by the plane variance multiplier.
- **step-wick-law** [claim](#stmt-thm-wick) / [proof](#proof-stmt-thm-wick): Green-function subtraction, maximum principle, Gaussian moment determination, and law uniqueness. -> Wick recursion and the unique Gaussian field law.
- **step-main-field-limit** [claim](#stmt-thm-main) / [proof](#proof-stmt-thm-wick): Apply tightness and the identified common subsequential law with the positive plane normalization. -> Weighted zero-Dirichlet Gaussian free field convergence and all mixed moments.

<a id="pm-s4"></a>
## 4. Engineering Triptych

### Panel 1 - epistemic contract

- **invariant-distributional-field-limit**: For a fixed admissible edge weight, the normalized height field converges as a random distribution to the zero-Dirichlet Gaussian free field. The normalization is positive and independent of the domain and its inside approximation; all mixed moments of smooth test pairings converge.
- **invariant-open-cell-factorization**: A prescribed good circuit separates the conditional laws on its sides. Strictly interior cells retain their original weights, and crossing cells impose no complementary-spin constraint. Fixing the complete inner height trace gives the ordinary weighted height Gibbs law.
- **invariant-restricted-history-association**: Positive association and conditional stochastic order hold for feasible histories that observe every first-spin site of each observed cell and leave complementary-spin component labels unobserved.
- **invariant-exact-zero-total-observables**: A zero-integral smooth test produces exactly zero-total face-area weights. Its height statistic therefore ignores the additive lift offset, and the area interpolation respects site reflections exactly.

### Panel 2 - negative knowledge

- **anti-pointwise-limit**: Treat convergence of smooth height pairings as convergence of individual site heights. -> Point variances grow logarithmically, while the theorem identifies a distribution-valued limit through smooth spatial averages.
- **anti-explicit-normalization**: Calibrate every edge weight using a supplied closed formula or a common normalization constant. -> The source establishes an implicit normalization for each fixed weight and does not identify its value by an explicit formula or assert independence from the weight.
- **anti-status-only-conditioning**: Condition on a closed cell status alone and reuse the association theorem. -> Such conditioning can produce negative first-spin pair covariance and falls outside the permitted history class.
- **anti-unopened-spin-cut**: Infer independence across a circuit merely from agreement of its first spins. -> First-spin agreement alone does not remove crossing complementary-spin interactions.
- **anti-reflection-variance-confusion**: Conclude that a Laplace insertion has vanishing ordinary variance from its vanishing reflection seminorm. -> The reflection seminorm tends to zero, but the ordinary second moment is only bounded and need not vanish.
- **anti-degenerating-geometry-uniformity**: Shrink obstacle gaps or boundary depths together with the mesh using fixed-geometry constants. -> The estimates may depend on the positive widths and separations fixed before the mesh limit.

### Panel 3 - reference implementation and oracle

Applicability: `not_applicable`. The target result is a continuum scaling limit of random distributions, requiring tightness, boundary control, collision identification, and Gaussian mixed moments over a mesh sequence tending to zero. The source states: “All mixed moments of these vectors converge.” Its normalization is implicit: “The theorem is for each fixed $x$; it neither specifies a formula for $\sigma(x)$ nor asserts that this constant is independent of $x$.” Finite checks of spin lifts or rounded midpoints would verify auxiliary constructions only and would not certify this field limit.

| software | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The field convergence theorem supplies an asymptotic mathematical specification but no software interface, implementation, or finite approximation error contract. |
| games_simulation | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The limit describes smoothly averaged random heights, while individual loop convergence is outside its conclusion. It supplies no dynamics for animated surfaces or interfaces. |
| tools | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The normalization is an implicit positive constant, so the theorem does not provide a parameter calibration tool with an explicit numerical output. |
| algorithms | True | moderate | adaptable | inferred | The integer-lift proof gives a finite construction: compute the prescribed increment on every oriented edge and integrate it from an anchored vertex. Vanishing triangular circulation makes the resulting height independent of the selected paths. |
| data_structures | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The closed-cell component graph describes conditional spin labels, but the paper establishes no storage representation, update procedure, or data-structure performance guarantee. |
| hardware_accelerators | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The positive normal transfer is an operator on a quotient Hilbert space. Its positivity and contraction property do not construct a hardware execution schedule or accelerator. |
| crypto_security | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The protected switch preserves Gibbs weights and changes a height lift while preserving protected spins. It provides no cryptographic hardness, secrecy, or adversarial security statement. |
| machine_learning | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The plane covariance identifies a limiting random-field covariance for zero-integral tests. The paper constructs no training procedure, predictor, or statistical learning guarantee. |
| optimisation_operations_research | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | Rounded midpoint admissibility and its energy inequality support moment bounds for a probability measure. They do not specify an optimization objective, search algorithm, or optimality certificate. |
| distributed_systems | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The online exploration preserves conditional Gibbs marginals through a finite recursive coupling. It does not address asynchronous communication, failures, or distributed agreement. |
| other (mathematical_physics) | True | strong | adaptable | inferred | The paper gives an exact finite construction of constant-boundary height configurations from disjoint honeycomb loops and their jump signs. This supports finite statistical-mechanics model construction alongside the asymptotic field theorem. |

## 6. Applicability limits and search

- **limit-fixed-parameter-regime** (hypothesis): The field theorem applies to each fixed edge weight in the stated closed interval. It does not establish the field limit outside that interval or uniform estimates as the weight varies. Blocked use: ['Extend the field convergence theorem to other edge weights.', 'Use the estimates uniformly over varying edge weights.']
- **limit-inside-smooth-domain-approximation** (hypothesis): The bounded-domain conclusion requires the specified simply connected smooth Jordan domain, inside exhaustion, and uniformly convergent boundary parametrizations. Blocked use: ['Apply the theorem to domains with holes or rough boundaries.', 'Replace boundary parametrization convergence by set convergence alone.']
- **limit-triangular-height-model** (formal_scope): The scaling theorem concerns integer Lipschitz heights on triangular face centers with zero boundary values and the specified weight for unequal adjacent pairs. Blocked use: ['Transfer the conclusion directly to square lattices, real-valued heights, or arbitrary graph models.', 'Change the microscopic slope constraint or edge interaction while retaining the conclusion.']
- **limit-zero-boundary-data** (formal_scope): The weighted theorem does not extend to the companion model's two-arc boundary data or identify the normalization constants of the distinct models. Blocked use: ['Use the weighted theorem as a two-arc boundary convergence theorem.', 'Reuse the companion normalization without an independent identification.']
- **limit-distributional-observables** (formal_scope): The limit is distribution-valued and tested through smooth spatial averages. It does not establish convergence of individual site heights. Blocked use: ['Treat the limiting field as a collection of pointwise height values.', 'Introduce logarithmic amplitude rescaling as part of the stated theorem.']
- **limit-implicit-normalization** (nonconstructive): The normalization is positive and domain-independent for each fixed weight, but the theorem supplies no formula for its dependence on that weight. Blocked use: ['Claim an explicit parameter calibration formula.', 'Assume a common amplitude normalization for different edge weights.']
- **limit-loop-ensemble-convergence** (formal_scope): The exact loop representation supports the height law; the field theorem does not assert convergence of individual loops or their ensemble. Blocked use: ['Certify interface or loop-ensemble convergence from the field theorem.']
- **limit-phase-diagram** (formal_scope): The predicted critical endpoint is identified as a literature prediction, and a sharp complete phase diagram is outside the theorem. Blocked use: ['Claim that the theorem determines every phase transition or behavior below the endpoint.']
- **limit-ambient-cycle-constraints** (hypothesis): The disk lift and wall factorization use triangular face boundaries to generate the relevant cycle constraints. Removing triangles to create holes without retaining additional cycle constraints invalidates that justification. Blocked use: ['Integrate coherent spin increments on a punctured graph using only local triangle checks.', 'Apply the wall factorization after deleting a hole and omitting its cycle constraints.']
- **limit-open-cut-prescriptions** (hypothesis): Exact separation requires a simple interior honeycomb circuit with prescribed signed open cells and no crossing equality edge. First-spin agreement alone is insufficient. Blocked use: ['Infer independence from a monochromatic first-spin circuit without open-cell prescriptions.', 'Use the cut while equality constraints connect its two sides.']
- **limit-complete-history-observations** (counterexample_scope): Conditional association requires observing every first-spin site of each observed cell. A closed-status observation alone can produce negative first-spin covariance; joint association also does not assert a lattice condition for the unsummed density. Blocked use: ['Reuse association after conditioning only on a closed status.', 'Replace joint association by a lattice-condition claim for the raw density.', 'Include arbitrary complementary-spin component labels in a permitted history.']
- **limit-stopped-retained-law** (hypothesis): Conditional plane matching requires an exact retained open-cut law with no additional inside pins or equality edges. Its record-independent plane copy requires the same conditional plane marginal on every exterior record, including failure. Blocked use: ['Claim record independence from an unconditional marginal match alone.', 'Reveal retained complementary-spin labels and still invoke the unlabelled retained-law comparison.', 'Apply the conditional matching result under arbitrary exterior spin-label conditioning without an exact cut.']
- **limit-fixed-buffer-order** (hypothesis): Widths, separations, and finite arrangements are fixed before taking the mesh limit. Gap closing, window shrinking, and boundary approaches occur afterward. Blocked use: ['Use fixed-geometry constants uniformly for collapsing buffers.', 'Couple a degenerating geometry to the mesh limit without a separate estimate.']
- **limit-rare-pin-comparison** (hypothesis): The multiplicative comparison requires disjoint filled neighborhoods, interior support clearance, and a fixed number of connected complementary-label requests. Constants may depend on those buffers and that label count. Blocked use: ['Divide an additive mixing error by a vanishing pin probability.', 'Claim geometry-independent comparison for colliding obstacles.', 'Let the connected label-request count grow while retaining the same constants.']
- **limit-protected-switch-orbits** (hypothesis): Protected switches require opposite nested good cuts and an unconstrained complementary component in the collar. Their equal-weight orbit identity survives invariant checks, but does not imply independence after arbitrary checks. Blocked use: ['Flip a prescribed component label and claim unchanged conditional weight.', 'Interpret the parity orbit identity as conditional independence under arbitrary offset tests.']
- **limit-full-trace-smearing-regime** (hypothesis): Bounded-trace smearing estimates retain every interaction up to the connected fixed skeleton and require the stated support radius, total absolute weight, and maximum coefficient bounds relative to boundary distance. Blocked use: ['Delete interactions incident to the trace and reuse the Gibbs estimates.', 'Apply the smearing estimate to concentrated site weights that violate its coefficient bound.', 'Use the bounded-trace estimate without fixing the complete inner height layer after a cut.']
- **limit-classwise-midpoint-central-mass** (hypothesis): Midpoint amplification requires admissible same-class outputs, the weight and rounding inequalities, and positive unconditional central mass in every input class. Central mass for the union of classes alone is insufficient. Blocked use: ['Apply amplification to an arbitrary spin-pinned ensemble without proving its parity-class conditions.', 'Replace classwise central mass by a central bound on the full support.', 'Impose extra support constraints without verifying both rounded outputs.']
- **limit-plane-zero-total-tests** (hypothesis): The plane moment and covariance statements concern zero-total or zero-integral tests, which remove the unspecified additive height offset. Exact face integrals preserve that cancellation at each mesh. Blocked use: ['Apply the plane increment estimates to an absolute-height average without an anchor.', 'Replace exact zero total by approximate cancellation without controlling the residual offset.']
- **limit-reflection-form-and-motion** (hypothesis): Reflection-null insertion concerns the reflection seminorm across site rows with separated same-side support. Analytic translation additionally requires strict projection gaps and at most one unbounded zero-total insertion. Blocked use: ['Conclude that the ordinary variance vanishes from reflection-nullity.', 'Use arbitrary reflection lines without the site-row construction.', 'Continue normalized expectations through colliding supports or uncontrolled unbounded factors.']
- **limit-checked-pins-and-gap-closing** (hypothesis): Separated checked-pin moments require free cut-search neighborhoods away from the obstacles. Their constants alone do not remain uniform as gaps close; the common-offset estimate supplies that separate control. Blocked use: ['Discard lifted-pair checks when invoking checked-pin moments.', 'Use separated-obstacle moment constants uniformly during gap collision.', 'Transfer insertion identities without the strict grid and middle-strip geometry.']
- **limit-real-boundary-traces** (hypothesis): Artificial openness applies only outside the original height problem. Real sites exposed or removed during an arch search retain their observed heights as usable trace data. Attachments and bulk tubes require their stated clean patches and clearances. Blocked use: ['Declare a real separator artificially open to obtain an arch.', 'Erase observed real trace values before applying a retained Gibbs law.', 'Replace a genuine boundary attachment by existence of a bulk circuit alone.']
- **limit-boundary-reference-order** (hypothesis): Boundary reference decorrelation fixes distinct boundary points and takes depth limits before increasing the number of references. The estimates do not supply mesh-uniform control for a depth moving with the approximation error. Blocked use: ['Approach colliding boundary points using the distinct-point decorrelation claim.', 'Increase the reference count before its fixed-point depth limit.', 'Let averaging depth track mesh error without further estimates.']
- **limit-cylinder-class-and-label-constraints** (hypothesis): Cylinder comparisons preserve the chosen cell-class boundary convention and use edge-disjoint selected cells. Port comparisons leave complementary labels unprescribed, and patch estimates require compatible extensions containing every cell incident to a mutable site. Blocked use: ['Identify the two cell-class laws at the same location.', 'Assert joint association for overlapping augmentations.', 'Use a patch probability bound for an incompatible opposite pin.', 'Remove exterior wiring while retaining arbitrary fixed complementary labels.']
- **limit-plus-layer-and-slide-direction** (hypothesis): The equality-insertion decrease requires both endpoints pinned plus. Boundary-slide inequalities have the stated directional order and cannot be replaced by a general claim that outward motion increases every event. Blocked use: ['Apply the plus-layer decrease to endpoints with an arbitrary common sign.', 'Reverse an upper favorable-cut slide while retaining its probability inequality.', 'Apply separated-path gluing to paths that lack the specified extremal separation.']
- **limit-full-law-identification** (formal_scope): Covariance identification alone is insufficient for the full Gaussian field conclusion. The proof also requires tightness, insertion transfer, boundary references, harmonic moments, exclusion of collision-supported distributions, and collision coefficients. Blocked use: ['Certify Gaussianity solely from the plane covariance.', 'Apply the off-diagonal harmonic formulas on collisions without the local-integrability identification.', 'Claim a full random-distribution law from isolated finite test checks.']
- **limit-no-finite-scaling-certificate** (nonconstructive): The continuum field theorem is established through limits and law identification. Finite checks of auxiliary lifts or midpoint inequalities cannot certify the complete scaling limit, and an effective finite-mesh error contract is ABSENT. Blocked use: ['Report finite auxiliary enumeration as a certificate for the continuum theorem.', 'Claim a computable mesh threshold for a requested field-law tolerance from the existence statement.']

<a id="pm-s7"></a>
## 7. Complete mathematical paper


We prove a Gaussian free field scaling limit for weighted integer Lipschitz heights on the triangular lattice. With zero boundary values and a factor <i>x</i> for each edge on which the height changes, the field converges after division by a positive constant depending only on <i>x</i> to the zero-Dirichlet Gaussian free field, for every fixed $`x\in[1/\sqrt2,1]`$. The convergence holds as a random distribution on every bounded <i>C</i><sup>2</sup> Jordan domain under inside lattice approximations with uniformly convergent boundary parametrizations. This includes the uniform height model and the predicted critical endpoint.

<a id="sec:introduction"></a>
### Introduction

An integer Lipschitz function on the triangular lattice is a discrete surface with a hard constraint on its nearest-neighbor slopes. We weight each unit height change by a parameter $x$. The associated contours form the loop $O(2)$ model on the hexagonal lattice. We prove that the smoothly averaged surface has a Gaussian free field limit throughout $1/\sqrt2\le x\le1$, including the predicted critical endpoint. The normalization is independent of the domain and of its lattice approximation.

<a id="pm-h-3"></a>
#### Model, approximation, and theorem

Let $\mathbb H$ be the hexagonal lattice embedded in $\mathbb R^2$ so that its face centers form the triangular lattice $$\mathbb T=\mathbb Z(1,0)+\mathbb Z(1/2,\sqrt3/2).$$ Two faces are adjacent when they share an edge. We identify each face with its center whenever using the triangular-lattice description.

<a id="stmt-def-approximation"></a>
<div id="def:approximation" class="definition">

**Definition 1** (Inside approximation). Let $D\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a bounded simply connected domain with $C^2$ Jordan boundary. For each mesh $\delta$ in a sequence tending to zero, let $\gamma_\delta$ be a simple cycle in $\delta\mathbb H$, let $D_\delta$ be its bounded interior, and include every lattice vertex and edge on or inside the cycle. We require $D_\delta\subset D$, that every compact subset of $D$ is eventually contained in $D_\delta$, and that there are parametrizations $$\gamma_\delta:S^1\longrightarrow\partial D_\delta,
 \qquad \gamma:S^1\longrightarrow\partial D,
 \qquad \|\gamma_\delta-\gamma\|_\infty\longrightarrow0.$$ Here each parametrization is a homeomorphism onto the indicated curve. Write $F_\delta$ for the hexagonal faces enclosed by $\gamma_\delta$, and $\partial F_\delta$ for those adjacent to the boundary cycle.

</div>

<a id="eq:model"></a>
Fix $x\in[1/\sqrt2,1]$. An admissible height is a function $h:F_\delta\to\mathbb Z$ such that $$h=0\quad\text{on }\partial F_\delta,
 \qquad |h(u)-h(v)|\le1\quad\text{whenever }u\sim v.$$ Its probability is $$\label{eq:model}
 \mathbb P_{\delta,x}(h)=\frac{x^{N_\delta(h)}}{Z_{\delta,x}},
 \qquad
 N_\delta(h)=\sum_{\{u,v\}\subset F_\delta:\,u\sim v}
                 \mathbf 1_{\{h(u)\ne h(v)\}}.$$ The sum counts each unordered adjacent pair once. The admissible set is finite, since the height at any face is bounded in absolute value by its graph distance to $\partial F_\delta$. It contains the zero function, so $Z_{\delta,x}$ is finite and positive. Height reflection preserves <a href="#eq:model" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:model">[eq:model]</a>; in particular, $\mathbb Eh_\delta(u)=0$.

Extend $h_\delta$ as a constant on each enclosed face and by zero outside $D_\delta$. For $f\in C_c^\infty(D)$ we always use the Euclidean area pairing <a id="eq:area-pairing"></a>$$\label{eq:area-pairing}
 h_\delta(f)=\int_D h_\delta(z)f(z)\,\mathrm dz
 =\sum_{u\in F_\delta} w_{\delta,f}(u)h_\delta(u),
 \qquad w_{\delta,f}(u)=\int_{\text{face at }u}f(z)\,\mathrm dz.$$ For small enough $\delta$, these weights sum to $\int_D f$ exactly.

Let $\Phi_D$ denote the real zero-Dirichlet Gaussian free field with covariance <a id="eq:gff-covariance"></a>$$\label{eq:gff-covariance}
 \mathbb E[\Phi_D(f)\Phi_D(g)]
 =\iint_{D\times D} f(z)G_D(z,w)g(w)\,\mathrm dz\,\mathrm dw,
 \qquad G_D=(-\Delta_D)^{-1}.$$ The Laplacian is the Euclidean Laplacian. Thus the singular part of $G_D(z,w)$ is $(2\pi)^{-1}\log(1/|z-w|)$.

<a id="stmt-thm-main"></a>
<div id="thm:main" class="theorem">

**Theorem 2**. *For every fixed $x\in[1/\sqrt2,1]$ there exists $\sigma(x)\in(0,\infty)$, independent of $D$ and of the inside approximation in Definition <a href="#def:approximation" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:approximation">1</a>, such that $$\frac{h_\delta}{\sigma(x)}\ \Longrightarrow\ \Phi_D
 \qquad\text{in }\mathcal D'(D).$$ In particular, the fields are tight as random distributions and, for every $k\ge1$ and $f_1,\ldots,f_k\in C_c^\infty(D)$, the vector $(h_\delta(f_i)/\sigma(x))_{i=1}^k$ converges to $(\Phi_D(f_i))_{i=1}^k$. All mixed moments of these vectors converge.*

</div>

There is no logarithmic rescaling of the amplitude. The logarithmic growth of point variances (Glazman and Lammers 2025, sec. 1.2.4) <a id="pm-cite-1"></a>[[GL2025](#ref-GL2025)] is compatible with finite fluctuations after smooth spatial averaging. The theorem is for each fixed $x$; it neither specifies a formula for $\sigma(x)$ nor asserts that this constant is independent of $x$.

The loop description is exact. At each interior vertex of $\mathbb H$, the three incident face heights have range at most one. Consequently either zero or two incident edges separate unequal heights. The occupied edges therefore form mutually vertex-disjoint loops away from the boundary cycle. Conversely, such a loop family, together with an independent choice of one of its two orientations for each loop, determines an admissible height by summing its signed nesting increments from the zero exterior. Thus its un-oriented weight is <a id="eq:loop-weight"></a>$$\label{eq:loop-weight}
 2^{\#\text{loops}}x^{\#\text{occupied edges}}.$$ Theorem <a href="#thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:main">2</a> concerns the field law; no convergence claim for the individual loops or their ensemble is needed.

<a id="pm-h-4"></a>
#### Context and significance

Schramm’s problem collection asks for Gaussian free field behavior of the uniform odd-integer Lipschitz height on the triangular lattice with two boundary arcs, and separately asks about its interface (Schramm 2007, Problem 2.2) <a id="pm-cite-2"></a>[[Schramm2007](#ref-Schramm2007)]. That formulation has a different boundary condition and height convention from <a href="#eq:model" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:model">[eq:model]</a>. It motivates the field question studied here. The real-valued model in his Problem 2.3 is another distinct model.

The loop description belongs to the classical solid-on-solid viewpoint: Nienhuis relates honeycomb loop weights to integer heights on the triangular lattice (Nienhuis 1982, 1062) <a id="pm-cite-3"></a>[[Nienhuis1982](#ref-Nienhuis1982)]. The predicted critical curve discussed in (Glazman and Lammers 2025, sec. 1.4.1) <a id="pm-cite-4"></a>[[GL2025](#ref-GL2025)] gives $x_c(2)=1/\sqrt2$. Throughout this paper, the phrase *predicted critical endpoint* refers to that prediction; a sharp description of the complete phase diagram is not part of the theorem.

At $x=1/\sqrt2$, macroscopic loops and the resulting logarithmic height variances were established by Duminil-Copin, Glazman, Peled and Spinka (Duminil-Copin et al. 2021, Theorem 1 and Section 1.2) <a id="pm-cite-5"></a>[[DGPS2021](#ref-DGPS2021)]. Glazman and Manolescu established logarithmic height variances for the uniform integer Lipschitz model and developed its two-spin representation and associated correlation and crossing estimates (Glazman and Manolescu 2021) <a id="pm-cite-6"></a>[[GM2021](#ref-GM2021)]. Glazman and Lammers proved delocalization and logarithmic variance estimates in a broader loop-parameter regime, and related these estimates to the predicted Gaussian free field limit (Glazman and Lammers 2025, sec. 1.2.4) <a id="pm-cite-7"></a>[[GL2025](#ref-GL2025)]. More recently, Glazman, Harel and Zelesko gave another proof of delocalization: for $n=2$ and every $x\in[1/\sqrt2,1]$, each translation-invariant loop Gibbs measure has infinitely many loops surrounding every face (Glazman, Harel, and Zelesko 2025, Theorem 2) <a id="pm-cite-8"></a>[[GHZ2025](#ref-GHZ2025)]. These are roughness results, distinct from the field limit proved here.

The proof develops the reflection and moment method of the companion article (OpenAI 2026a, secs. 5, 7, 9, and 10) <a id="pm-cite-9"></a>[[UniformIntegerGFF](#ref-UniformIntegerGFF)] for the weighted family <a href="#eq:model" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:model">[eq:model]</a>. That article treats uniform odd integer heights with two boundary arcs. Table <a href="#tab:integer-models" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="tab:integer-models">1</a> records the different inputs and conclusions. The two-spin representation of Glazman–Manolescu and the weighted percolation augmentation of Glazman–Lammers provide the starting point for the conditional cuts (Glazman and Manolescu 2021; Glazman and Lammers 2025) <a id="pm-cite-10"></a>[[GM2021](#ref-GM2021), [GL2025](#ref-GL2025)]. The extension requires order inequalities after restricted observations and estimates for moments conditioned on rare weighted pinning events. We prove these statements below and give the ensuing spectral, boundary, and moment arguments in full.

<div id="tab:integer-models">

|               | Uniform two-arc companion                         | Present weighted model                                                      |
|:--------------|:--------------------------------------------------|:----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Height        | Odd integers, adjacent differences $0$ or $2$     | Integers, adjacent differences at most $1$                                  |
| Law           | Uniform; $H=(h-1)/2$ gives unit-weight increments | Weight $x$ for each unequal adjacent pair                                   |
| Boundary      | Two marked arcs with values $+1$ and $-1$         | Zero on the boundary layer of an inside approximation                       |
| Cuts          | Uniform spin cuts and loop estimates              | The $x$-dependent open-cell table and complete first-color/status histories |
| Normalization | An absolutely convergent finite-volume series     | An implicit positive constant $\sigma(x)$ for each fixed $x$                |
| Limit         | Harmonic boundary profile plus a Dirichlet GFF    | A zero-Dirichlet GFF                                                        |

The two integer-height articles retain separate model-specific proofs. The common reflection, pin-motion, and moment strategy does not identify their normalization constants or extend the weighted theorem to two-arc boundary data.

</div>

Reflection positivity provides a classical route from spatial symmetries to positive transfer operators; see Fröhlich–Israel–Lieb–Simon (Fröhlich et al. 1978) <a id="pm-cite-11"></a>[[FILS1978](#ref-FILS1978)] and the spectral discussion of Usui (Usui 2012, secs. 3–4) <a id="pm-cite-12"></a>[[Usui2012](#ref-Usui2012)]. Here the original edge interaction factorizes across a row of sites. We prove the associated positive normal transfer, including its phase-augmented form, directly. Appendix <a href="#sec:scalar-spectra" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:scalar-spectra">8</a> constructs the scalar measures needed for its Cauchy representation and for analytic translation.

The six-vertex GFF theorem of Duminil-Copin, Kozlowski, Lammers, and Manolescu provides substantial methodological precedents through transfer spectra, analytic translation, and harmonic multipoint functions (Duminil-Copin et al. 2026, sec. 4.5; Lemma 7.4; Section 7.2) <a id="pm-cite-13"></a>[[DCKLM2026](#ref-DCKLM2026)]. Their result concerns a full-plane zero-slope state on the square lattice for $a=b=1$ and $c\in[\sqrt3,2]$. Its covariance normalization uses surface tension and Bethe ansatz. Our plane coefficient is fixed by a three-mirror angular identity and a signed cutoff limit; the passage to the actual bounded-domain boundary additionally uses weighted rare-pin comparisons and boundary attachment. The final collision-to-moment argument also has a precedent in Kenyon’s identification of dimer-height correlations (Kenyon 2001, Lemma 3.1 and Proposition 3.2) <a id="pm-cite-14"></a>[[Kenyon2001](#ref-Kenyon2001)]. In the present model the collision coefficient comes from conditional local matching and logarithmic harmonic expansions.

A related six-vertex result (OpenAI 2026b, Theorem 1.1) <a id="pm-cite-15"></a>[[BalancedSixVertexGFF2026](#ref-BalancedSixVertexGFF2026)] establishes the GFF limit for $a=b=1$ and every fixed $c\in(0,2]$, in the zero-slope plane law defined by its prescribed iterated limit of balanced tori.

The conclusion strengthens logarithmic variance estimates to a limit law for the entire distribution-valued field. Identifying a covariance is only one part of this conclusion: the proof also establishes Gaussian higher moments, the zero boundary condition, and tightness. The parameter interval includes both the uniform height model $x=1$ and its predicted critical endpoint $x=1/\sqrt2$.

<a id="pm-h-5"></a>
#### Structure of the proof

<a id="pm-h-6"></a>
###### Exact weighted cuts and conditional order.

Section <a href="#sec:discrete" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:discrete">2</a> encodes a height modulo four by two spins and augments each upward triangular cell with a status. An open circuit fixes the first spin while leaving the second spin free. The resulting cell factorization gives an exact conditional cut. The order statement is proved for histories which record every first-spin site of an observed cell. This restriction is essential: conditioning on a status alone need not preserve positive association. Stopped explorations then give local mixing and multiplicative comparisons for separated pins.

<a id="pm-h-7"></a>
###### Uniform moments and the plane coefficient.

Section <a href="#sec:moments" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:moments">3</a> proves moment bounds for smeared heights, including irregular domains exposed by explorations. A discrete midpoint inequality of Klartag–Lehec (Klartag and Lehec 2019, Theorem 1.4) <a id="pm-cite-16"></a>[[KlartagLehec2019](#ref-KlartagLehec2019)], in the nonnegative-function form of (Gozlan et al. 2021, Theorem 3) <a id="pm-cite-17"></a>[[GRST2019](#ref-GRST2019)], amplifies central probability bounds to all moments. We derive the finite-support zero case directly from (Gozlan et al. 2021, Theorem 8) <a id="pm-cite-18"></a>[[GRST2019](#ref-GRST2019)], then verify the multidimensional application and rounding conditions explicitly. In Section <a href="#sec:plane" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:plane">4</a>, site reflection positivity gives a positive normal transfer operator. Its covariance is a mixture of Cauchy kernels in normal frequency. An angular identity using all three mirror directions forces every scaling limit of the spectral measure to be $c\,\,\mathrm dp/|p|^2$. A signed cutoff identity proves uniqueness of $c$, and a two-disk variance bound proves $c>0$. With our Fourier convention, <a id="eq:normalization"></a>$$\label{eq:normalization}
 v=(2\pi)^2c,\qquad \sigma(x)=\sqrt v.$$

<a id="pm-h-8"></a>
###### Pins, reflection, and the true boundary.

Section <a href="#sec:pins" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:pins">5</a> compares the field with upper and lower pinning brackets. Uniform normalized moment bounds allow analytic movement of separated pins in three directions. Averaging their phases and then closing the gaps transfers the reflection-null Laplace insertion from the plane to these brackets. Section <a href="#sec:boundary" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:boundary">6</a> proves the boundary attachment estimate: a synthetic boundary law gives a favorable level path, and a deterministic attachment argument connects it to the required boundary segment. Iterating in tubes yields boundary arches, makes the bracket means vanish, and controls boundary reference averages.

<a id="pm-h-9"></a>
###### Harmonic moments and the full field law.

Section <a href="#sec:limit" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:limit">7</a> first establishes distributional tightness and uniform integrability. The ordered coupling and the vanishing bracket means then identify the bracket limits with the true field and transfer the insertion identity to it. The insertion and boundary references make every limiting moment distribution separately harmonic away from collisions. Logarithmic moment bounds exclude distributions supported on the diagonals. Local comparison with the plane fixes the coefficient of every collision singularity. Subtracting the corresponding Green functions gives Wick’s recursion, which determines the Gaussian law. This completes the proof of Theorem <a href="#thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:main">2</a>.

<a id="pm-h-10"></a>
#### Conventions

The parameter $x$ is fixed. Constants may depend on $x$ and on a stated fixed macroscopic arrangement; this dependence is not asserted to be uniform over the parameter interval. The symbols $C,c,\alpha$ denote positive constants whose value may change between occurrences. A test at radius $r$ has support in a ball of that radius and magnitude $O(r^{-2})$. A zero-total test has integral zero. On the full plane we use $$\widehat f(p)=\int_{\mathbb R^2}e^{-ip\cdot z}f(z)\,\mathrm dz,
 \qquad
 \langle f,(-\Delta)^{-1}g\rangle
 =\frac1{(2\pi)^2}\int_{\mathbb R^2}
       \frac{\overline{\widehat f(p)}\widehat g(p)}{|p|^2}\,\mathrm dp$$ for real smooth compactly supported zero-total tests. The symbol $H$ denotes a generic integer lift in the discrete representations; it is distinct from the hexagonal lattice $\mathbb H$.

Every argument involving collars, windows, disks, or tubes first fixes their positive macroscopic widths and separations, then sends $\delta\downarrow0$. Limits that close gaps, shrink windows, or approach the boundary are taken afterward. A bound for fixed geometry is not used uniformly for a degenerating geometry. Explorations are stopped before inspecting the interior region whose conditional Gibbs law is subsequently used.

<a id="sec:discrete"></a>
### Exact cuts and conditional comparison

Throughout this section $x\in[1/\sqrt2,1]$ is fixed. We first work in lattice units. A finite ambient graph $G=(V,E)$ is a connected induced subgraph of $\mathbb T$ whose bounded faces are elementary triangles and whose union is a topological disk. We can always take a large regular hexagon. Holes in a height domain will be represented by fixed sites in such an ambient graph, rather than by deleting triangles. This distinction is needed in the wall factorization below.

The cell representation below will provide three conclusions: an exact conditional factorization across open circuits, order under observations that record a cell together with all its first-spin sites, and a multiplicative comparison for separated pin events. The last comparison remains useful when each pin event has probability tending to zero. We first construct the cell law whose open circuits make all three statements possible.

<a id="pm-h-12"></a>
#### Spins, cells, and exact cuts

<a id="discrete:gray"></a>
<a id="discrete:pair-weight"></a>
Associate to an integer $H$ the two spins $(B,W)$ given by $$\label{discrete:gray}
\begin{array}{c|cccc}
H\pmod4&0&1&2&3\\ \hline
(B,W)&(+,+)&(+,-)&(-,-)&(-,+).
\end{array}$$ Call a spin pair coherent if on each edge at least one of its two spins is constant. Its free weight on $G$ is $$\label{discrete:pair-weight}
 \prod_{uv\in E}x^{\mathbf 1\{(B_u,W_u)\ne(B_v,W_v)\}}\,
 \mathbf 1\{(B,W)\text{ is coherent}\}.$$ All ambient finite-volume laws in this section use this edge convention.

<a id="stmt-lem-spin-lift"></a>
<div id="lem:spin-lift" class="lemma">

<a id="discrete:increment"></a>
**Lemma 3** (Integer lift). *Every coherent pair on $G$ has an integer Lipschitz lift, unique up to addition of a multiple of four once the correspondence <a href="#discrete:gray" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="discrete:gray">[discrete:gray]</a> is fixed. For the oriented edge $uv$ its increment is $$\label{discrete:increment}
 H_v-H_u=\frac{W_uB_v-B_uW_v}{2}.$$ The free spin law induces the weighted height-increment law with one height anchored. Fixing a constant pair on a connected skeleton, and fixing the lift there, induces the usual weighted height Gibbs law in each bounded face of the skeleton.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-lem-spin-lift"><summary>Proof of stmt-lem-spin-lift</summary>

*Proof.* The right side of <a href="#discrete:increment" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="discrete:increment">[discrete:increment]</a> is $0$, $1$, or $-1$, and has the required residue in <a href="#discrete:gray" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="discrete:gray">[discrete:gray]</a>. A triangle cannot have both spins nonconstant: each nonconstant binary spin changes on two triangle edges, and these two pairs of edges must intersect. If $B$ is constant on a triangle, <a href="#discrete:increment" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="discrete:increment">[discrete:increment]</a> is $-B\,dW/2$ there; if $W$ is constant, it is $W\,dB/2$. Its circulation therefore vanishes. Every cycle of the triangulated disk is a sum of its triangle boundaries, so the increments integrate to $H$. The four choices of the anchor residue give four equally weighted spin representations of each anchored increment configuration: cyclic rotation of the states in <a href="#discrete:gray" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="discrete:gray">[discrete:gray]</a> preserves all increments and the weight. Finally each disagreeing pair contributes exactly one factor $x$. Fixing the connected trace fixes the lift on the whole skeleton, and the remaining edge factors are precisely those of the height Gibbs specification. ◻

</details>

<a id="discrete:cell-table"></a>
Let $Y$ be the centers of the upward-pointing elementary triangles, viewed as one partite class of the dual honeycomb lattice. Each primal edge belongs to exactly one such triangle. At the ambient boundary a cell can be clipped to a single edge; cells containing at most one site have no interaction. For an interacting cell $y$ write $V_y$ for its two or three sites and put $$q_y=\begin{cases}x^2,&|V_y|=3,\\ x,&|V_y|=2.\end{cases}$$ Introduce an open/closed variable by the following joint weights: $$\label{discrete:cell-table}
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
 \text{status}&\text{allowed spins}&\text{weight}\\ \hline
 \text{open}&B\text{ constant on }V_y,\ W\text{ arbitrary}&q_y\\
 \text{closed}&B,W\text{ both constant on }V_y&1-q_y\\
 \text{closed}&B\text{ nonconstant},\ W\text{ constant on }V_y&q_y.
\end{array}$$ An open cell is denoted $+$ or $-$ according to its constant $B$ value, and a closed cell is denoted $0$; thus $\tau_y\in\{-,0,+\}$. An interior nonconstant triangle has two changing edges. Summing <a href="#discrete:cell-table" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="discrete:cell-table">[discrete:cell-table]</a> consequently gives <a href="#discrete:pair-weight" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="discrete:pair-weight">[discrete:pair-weight]</a>, including the clipped edge convention.

We permit arbitrary deterministic $B$ pins and deterministic equalities $W_u=W_v$ on a set $E_0\subset E$. These equalities are not prescribed component labels. Given $(B,\tau)$, form the graph containing the edges of all closed cells and all edges of $E_0$, with isolated sites included. The conditional $W$ law labels its connected components by independent fair signs. In particular, if $m$ connected subgraphs have already been required to have constant $W$, the conditional probability that all their labels are plus lies in $[2^{-m},1]$. This includes singleton subgraphs and allows several prescribed subgraphs to belong to the same component.

A honeycomb edge is *authorized with sign $s$* if its endpoint in $Y$ has $\tau_y=s$. A good path or circuit of sign $s$ uses authorized edges. We only use these paths away from clipped ambient cells. The faces adjacent to a good path have $B=s$ and their connected face chain therefore has a height trace in one pair of consecutive integers. A nearest-neighbor path of good $Y$ vertices can be converted into a honeycomb walk by joining successive vertices through their common honeycomb neighbor. The displacement is bounded in lattice units. A closed walk with nonzero winding around a target contains a simple surrounding circuit. All geometric constructions below have positive clearance, so this conversion preserves their requirements for sufficiently fine mesh.

<div class="samepage">

<a id="stmt-lem-cell-cut"></a>
<div id="lem:cell-cut" class="lemma">

**Lemma 4** (Open-cell cut). *Let $\gamma$ be a simple honeycomb circuit strictly inside the ambient graph. Prescribe $\tau_y=s$ at every $y\in Y\cap\gamma$. Suppose no edge of $E_0$ crosses $\gamma$. Conditional on these prescriptions and any deterministic constraints on the two respective sides, the two sides are independent after their prescribed first-spin layers are identified. On the inside, all cells centered strictly inside retain their original weights; crossing cells contribute constants and impose no condition on $W$. This inside law depends only on $\gamma$, $s$, and the constraints inside. Given the complete height trace of the inside boundary layer, its free sites have the ordinary weighted height Gibbs law, with any additional inside constraints retained.*

</div>

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-lem-cell-cut"><summary>Proof of stmt-lem-cell-cut</summary>

*Proof.* Every interacting cell meeting both sides has its honeycomb center on $\gamma$. Its open prescription fixes every incident first spin to $s$, and its factor in <a href="#discrete:cell-table" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="discrete:cell-table">[discrete:cell-table]</a> is the constant $q_y$ for every choice of its second spins. All remaining factors involve sites on one side only. Equality edges do not cross by assumption. The product weight and its partition sum thus factor. In particular, complementary components cannot cross the circuit. After specifying the complete inner height layer, the spin lift and the edge weights in Lemma <a href="#lem:spin-lift" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:spin-lift">3</a> give the claimed height specification. No first-spin agreement event without the open-cell prescriptions has been used in this factorization. ◻

</details>

<figure id="discrete:fig-cut">

<figcaption>An exact open-cell cut. In (a), prescribing $B = +$ and $τ_{y} = +$ gives the constant cell weight $q = x^{2}$ for every second-spin assignment. In (b), filled circuit vertices are open-plus $Y$ cells; plus signs mark their prescribed first-spin sites. The tested exterior is shaded. No equality edge crosses $γ$, and the unobserved second spins have no component joining its two sides. Strictly interior cells retain their original interactions.</figcaption>
</figure>

<div class="samepage">

Here is the crossing estimate used throughout the discrete argument. Appendix <a href="#sec:annulus" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:annulus">9</a> gives its annulus proof. The boundary convention in its statement is part of the theorem.

<a id="stmt-thm-circuit-input"></a>
<div id="thm:circuit-input" class="theorem">

**Theorem 5** (Annulus circuit estimate). *For $r\ge0$, let $\Lambda_r$ be the ball of radius $r$ in the triangular graph metric, with its bounding honeycomb contour; thus $\Lambda_r=\Lambda_{\lfloor r\rfloor}$. For $a>1$ and an integer $n\in\mathbb N$, consider on $\Lambda_{an}$ the cell spin law whose interior cells have weight $(x^2)^{\mathbf 1\{B\text{ or }W\text{ nonconstant}\}}$ and whose boundary $Y$ cells are excluded. Fix $B=-$ on the boundary face layer and leave $W$ free. There is $c=c(x,a)>0$ such that, for $n\ge 3/(a-1)$, the probability of an occupied open-plus cell circuit surrounding $\Lambda_n$ and contained in $\Lambda_{an}$ is at least $c$. The same statement holds with the signs or the two spin colors interchanged.*

</div>

</div>

The conclusion is equation (55) in Appendix A of the third arXiv version of (Glazman and Lammers 2025) <a id="pm-cite-19"></a>[[GL2025](#ref-GL2025)], with Definitions 3.2 and 3.5. Its augmentation includes a cell whenever $W$ is nonconstant, excludes it whenever $B$ is nonconstant, and otherwise includes it with probability $x^2$. It is therefore exactly <a href="#discrete:cell-table" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="discrete:cell-table">[discrete:cell-table]</a>. The source uses $Y(\Omega)=(Y\cap V(\Omega))\setminus V(\partial\Omega)$; simply pinning $B=-$ in our edge-weight law would still charge certain boundary $W$ changes. Lemma <a href="#lem:cell-cut" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:cell-cut">4</a> instead identifies the source law with the law inside a prescribed regular open-minus circuit: the excluded boundary factors become constants. This is also the conditional law described by Lemma 3.8 of (Glazman and Lammers 2025) <a id="pm-cite-20"></a>[[GL2025](#ref-GL2025)]. We use the theorem only through this exact identification, with fixed slack for lattice rounding. In particular its validity includes $x=1/\sqrt2$.

<a id="pm-h-13"></a>
#### Restricted histories and the two-law inequality

A *history* fixes some first-spin sites and some cell statuses, with the rule that it fixes *all* first-spin sites of every observed cell. The equality set $E_0$ remains deterministic. No second-spin component labels are part of a history. Order first spins by $-<+$ and statuses by $-<0<+$. Ordered histories have the same observation sets and ordered values. They may also have additional deterministic plus $B$ pins only in the upper law, or additional deterministic minus $B$ pins only in the lower law, compatible with the common pins.

<a id="stmt-prop-history-order"></a>
<div id="prop:history-order" class="proposition">

**Proposition 6** (Association and conditional order). *For every feasible history, the unobserved $(B,\tau)$ variables are positively associated. Two laws with ordered histories and common $E_0$ are stochastically ordered, including the unequal extreme pins just described. Extra prescribed open-plus cells only in the upper law, or open-minus cells only in the lower law, can be incorporated by observing those cells and all their first-spin sites also in the other law. These claims hold for clipped cells and at $x=1$.*

</div>

We first prove two finite-weight inequalities used in the proof of this proposition, then apply them to the cell law.

We use the finite association inequality of Fortuin–Kasteleyn–Ginibre (Fortuin, Kasteleyn, and Ginibre 1971) <a id="pm-cite-21"></a>[[FKG1971](#ref-FKG1971)], including weights that vanish. Its precise form follows from the rounded-midpoint inequality stated and tensorized in Theorem <a href="#thm:midpoint" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:midpoint">18</a>: for nonnegative finitely supported arrays, the premise $f(b)g(c)\le u(\lfloor(b+c)/2\rfloor)v(\lceil(b+c)/2\rceil)$ implies $(\sum f)(\sum g)\le(\sum u)(\sum v)$. Indeed, on a Boolean cube the rounded midpoints of $b,c$ are their coordinatewise minimum $b\wedge c$ and maximum $b\vee c$. If a nonnegative weight $w$ satisfies $w(b)w(c)\le w(b\wedge c)w(b\vee c)$ and $F,G$ are nonnegative increasing functions, then $$w(b)F(b)w(c)G(c)
 \le w(b\wedge c)w(b\vee c)F(b\vee c)G(b\vee c).$$ Apply the midpoint inequality to $wF,wG,w,wFG$, extended by zero outside the cube. Its conclusion is $(\sum wF)(\sum wG)\le(\sum w)(\sum wFG)$, which is association after normalization. Encode an element of a finite chain by a prefix of ones followed by zeros. The encoded product of chains is closed under minimum and maximum, so extension by zero proves the same result there. Adding constants to bounded increasing functions covers signed functions. This deduction explains every finite association use below; the midpoint tensorization itself uses no association statement.

The wall decomposition below expresses the first-spin weight using two partition sums for the complementary spin. We record the two properties of those sums needed to compare first-spin configurations.

<a id="stmt-discrete-ising-partition"></a>
<div id="discrete:ising-partition" class="lemma">

<a id="discrete:Z-lattice"></a>
**Lemma 7** (The complementary-spin partition sum). *For $a\in[0,1]^E$ define <a id="discrete:ising-Z"></a>$$\label{discrete:ising-Z}
 Z(a)=\sum_{\sigma\in\{-,+\}^{V}}
             \prod_{e=uv\in E}a_e^{\mathbf 1\{\sigma_u\ne\sigma_v\}},
 \qquad 0^0=1.$$ Then $Z$ is increasing in every coordinate and is log-supermodular: $$\label{discrete:Z-lattice}
 Z(a\wedge b)Z(a\vee b)\ge Z(a)Z(b).$$*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-discrete-ising-partition"><summary>Proof of stmt-discrete-ising-partition</summary>

*Proof.* Monotonicity follows term by term. For positive coordinates the second assertion follows by differentiating in $\log a_e$. For distinct edges $e=uv$ and $f=st$, $$\frac{\partial^2\log Z}{\partial\log a_e\,\partial\log a_f}
 =\mathop{\mathrm{Cov}}(\mathbf 1\{\sigma_u\ne\sigma_v\},
              \mathbf 1\{\sigma_s\ne\sigma_t\})
